ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.q: Which part of a computer processes instructions and is often called its brain?
ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.why: The CPU carries out program instructions and calculations.

ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.q: What is the main job of an operating system such as Windows?
options: To connect the ship to satellites
To manage the hardware and run programs
To protect the screen from dust
ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.why: The operating system controls the hardware and lets applications run.

ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.q: What happens to unsaved work when the computer suddenly loses power?
options: It moves to the Recycle Bin
It is saved automatically to the hard disk
ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.why: Unsaved work is held in RAM, which loses its contents without power.

ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.q: What is the best way to organize files on a shipboard computer?
options: Keep only one file per computer
Use clearly named folders and file names
ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.why: Clear folders and names make files easy to find and hard to lose.

ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.q: What does the Cc field in an email do?
options: Sends a copy to other recipients
ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.why: Cc (carbon copy) sends a copy of the email to additional recipients.

ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.q: Which program is best for a table of calculations such as a stores inventory?
ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.why: Spreadsheets like Excel are made for tables, formulas and totals.

ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.q: Which of these is the strongest password?
ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.why: A long mix of upper and lower case letters, numbers and symbols is hardest to guess.

ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.q: Why should you make regular backups of important files?
options: To make the computer run faster
To recover data if files are lost or damaged
ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.why: Backups let you restore files after deletion, damage or a virus.

ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.q: What should you do with an email attachment from an unknown sender?
options: Open it immediately to check it
Do not open it and report it to the responsible officer
Forward it to all crew members
Save it to a USB drive for later
ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.why: Unknown attachments may contain malware, so they should not be opened.

ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.q: What is the keyboard shortcut to copy selected text in Windows?
ABC - Awareness on Basic Computer.why: Ctrl + C copies; Ctrl + V pastes, Ctrl + Z undoes and Ctrl + P prints.

AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.q: What is harassment in the workplace?
options: A disagreement that is settled politely
A friendly joke that both people enjoy
Unwanted behavior that offends, humiliates or intimidates a person
A normal work instruction from a superior
AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.why: Harassment is unwanted conduct that violates a person's dignity or creates a hostile environment.

options: Repeated unreasonable behavior aimed at a person or group
A safety drill ordered by the Master
A single polite correction of someone's work
A request to work paid overtime
AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.why: Bullying is repeated, unreasonable behavior that can harm a person's health and safety.

AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.q: A crew member tells you privately they were sexually harassed. What should you do first?
options: Tell the whole crew at the next meeting
Ignore it unless there is a witness
Ask them to settle it with the harasser alone
Listen, take it seriously and follow the reporting procedure
AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.why: Reports must be taken seriously and handled through the company's procedure.

AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.q: Why is confidentiality important when handling a harassment report?
options: It protects the people involved and encourages reporting
It avoids having to write any records
It hides the incident from the company
It allows the case to be quietly forgotten
AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.why: Confidentiality protects victims and witnesses so people feel safe to report.

AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.q: Which international convention sets seafarers' rights to decent working and living conditions?
AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.why: The MLC, 2006 is the seafarers' bill of rights for working and living conditions.

AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.q: Under the MLC, 2006, what must seafarers have access to onboard?
options: A private cabin for every rating
AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.why: MLC Regulation 5.1.5 requires on-board procedures for fair and quick handling of complaints.

options: Transferring a seafarer at contract end
Punishing someone for reporting or supporting a complaint
Giving positive feedback to a coworker
AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.why: Retaliation against people who report is itself misconduct and must be prevented.

AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.q: What should a bystander who sees harassment do?
options: Safely intervene or report it to a superior or designated person
Record it and post it on social media
Wait until they are called as a witness
AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.why: Bystanders help stop harassment by acting safely or reporting it.

AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.q: Which is an example of sexual harassment?
options: Asking a colleague to attend a drill
Correcting a mistake in the logbook
Assigning a crew member to their scheduled watch
Repeated unwanted comments about a person's body
AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.why: Unwanted remarks of a sexual nature about someone's body are sexual harassment.

AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.q: What is the main goal of a harassment prevention policy onboard?
options: Reducing the number of crew onboard
A safe and respectful working environment for everyone
AHPR - Awareness on Harassment Preventio.why: The policy aims to prevent harm and ensure every seafarer is treated with respect.

AI - Accident Investigation.q: What is the main purpose of a marine accident investigation?
options: To find the causes and prevent recurrence
AI - Accident Investigation.why: Safety investigations aim to learn lessons and prevent similar accidents, not to blame.

AI - Accident Investigation.q: Once an accident is under control, why should the scene be preserved?
options: To allow repairs to start at once
To keep evidence unchanged for the investigation
To make the area look clean for visitors
AI - Accident Investigation.why: Moving or cleaning items can destroy evidence needed to find the cause.

AI - Accident Investigation.q: Which section of the ISM Code covers reports and analysis of accidents and hazardous occurrences?
AI - Accident Investigation.why: ISM Code Section 9 requires reporting, investigation and analysis of non-conformities, accidents and hazardous occurrences.

AI - Accident Investigation.q: Which shipboard equipment records data useful for reconstructing a navigation accident?
AI - Accident Investigation.why: The VDR stores bridge audio, radar, position and other data from before an incident.

options: Separately and as soon as possible
Using leading questions to save time
Only at the end of the contract
AI - Accident Investigation.why: Separate, early interviews give fresh accounts that are not influenced by others.

options: An event that could have caused harm but did not
AI - Accident Investigation.why: A near miss is an unplanned event with potential for harm where no harm occurred.

AI - Accident Investigation.q: Why should near misses be reported?
options: They give lessons before an actual accident happens
To increase paperwork for the crew
To meet a monthly quota only
AI - Accident Investigation.why: Near misses reveal hazards early so they can be fixed before someone is hurt.

AI - Accident Investigation.q: Damaged parts, broken equipment and fluid samples are examples of what type of evidence?
AI - Accident Investigation.why: Physical evidence is the actual objects and materials from the scene.

AI - Accident Investigation.q: When is a corrective action effective?
options: When it names the person to blame
When it only replaces the damaged part
When it is written but not followed up
When it removes or controls the cause so the event does not recur
AI - Accident Investigation.why: An effective action addresses the cause and is verified to work.

AI - Accident Investigation.q: Which document records the findings and recommendations of an investigation?
AI - Accident Investigation.why: The investigation report presents the facts, causes and recommended actions.

AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.q: In risk assessment, what is a hazard?
options: Anything with the potential to cause harm
The chance that harm will happen
AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.why: A hazard is a source of potential harm; risk is how likely and how severe the harm may be.

AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.q: Risk is commonly assessed by combining which two factors?
AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.why: Risk = likelihood of an event x severity of its consequence.

AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.q: In the hierarchy of controls, which control is the most effective?
AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.why: Removing the hazard completely is the most effective control.

AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.q: In the hierarchy of controls, which control is the least effective?
AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.why: PPE is the last line of defense because it depends on correct use and does not remove the hazard.

options: The risk to the cargo only
The risk that exists only in port
The risk that remains after controls are applied
AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.why: Residual risk is what is left after control measures; it must be acceptable before work starts.

AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.q: Under the ISM Code, the company's safety management objectives include:
options: Assessing all identified risks and establishing safeguards
AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.why: ISM Code 1.2.2 requires the company to assess identified risks to ship, personnel and environment and set safeguards.

AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.q: When should a risk assessment be reviewed?
options: Only when the ship is sold
When conditions change or after an incident
AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.why: Risk assessments must be kept current when the task, conditions or lessons learned change.

AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.q: A Job Hazard Analysis divides the work into:
options: A list of crew names only
Steps, with hazards and controls for each step
AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.why: Breaking a job into steps helps identify hazards and controls for each part of the task.

AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.q: In an investigation, what is the root cause?
options: The underlying reason that, if fixed, prevents recurrence
The first person who saw the event
The last action before the accident
AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.why: Fixing the root cause stops the same type of accident happening again.

AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.q: Before high-risk work such as hot work or enclosed space entry, what is normally required?
options: Verbal permission from any crew member
Nothing if the job is short
A permit to work supported by a risk assessment
A note posted in the galley
AI-RA - Accident Investigation and Risk.why: Permit-to-work systems ensure hazards are checked and controls are in place before high-risk work.

AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.q: What is an event timeline used for in an investigation?
options: Showing events in the order they happened
AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.why: A timeline puts events in sequence so causes and missed barriers can be seen.

AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.q: What is the immediate cause of an accident?
options: The act or condition that directly led to the event
AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.why: The immediate cause is the direct trigger; deeper causes lie behind it.

options: Asking why repeatedly to reach the underlying cause
Taking five photos of the scene
AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.why: Repeatedly asking why moves from symptoms to the underlying cause.

AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.q: The fishbone diagram used in root cause analysis is also called the:
AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.why: The Ishikawa diagram groups possible causes into categories leading to the problem.

AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.q: Where are systemic causes usually found?
options: Only in the brand of equipment
In management systems, procedures and organization
Only in the weather at the time
AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.why: Systemic causes are weaknesses in the system that allowed the error or failure.

AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.q: Why is stopping an investigation at human error usually not enough?
options: It takes too much time to write
It does not explain why the error happened
It is not allowed in reports
AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.why: Finding why the person made the error reveals the fix that prevents recurrence.

AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.q: What makes a corrective action verifiable?
options: It is kept secret from the crew
It is written in very general words
It has a clear owner, deadline and way to check completion
AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.why: Clear ownership, timing and a check let the company confirm the action was done and works.

AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.q: Which of these is an example of a systemic cause?
options: The deck was wet at the time of the slip
A light bulb failed during the watch
A crew member dropped a spanner
No written procedure existed for the task
AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.why: A missing procedure is an organizational weakness that can lead to many incidents.

AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.q: What should be done after corrective actions are put in place?
AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.why: Follow-up confirms the actions actually prevent recurrence.

AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.q: What should be done with lessons learned from an investigation?
options: Share them with the crew and fleet
Share them only with the insurer
Keep them only with the Master
AIIRCA - Accident Investigation and Root.why: Sharing lessons helps other ships avoid the same incident.

AIS - Automatic Identification System.q: What is the main purpose of AIS?
options: To automatically exchange ship identification and navigation data
AIS - Automatic Identification System.why: AIS broadcasts and receives ship identity, position, course and speed to improve safety.

AIS - Automatic Identification System.q: On which radio band does shipborne AIS operate?
AIS - Automatic Identification System.why: AIS uses dedicated VHF maritime channels.

AIS - Automatic Identification System.q: Which of these is static AIS information?
AIS - Automatic Identification System.why: Static data such as name, call sign, MMSI and IMO number does not change during the voyage.

AIS - Automatic Identification System.q: Where does most dynamic AIS information come from?
options: Ship's sensors such as GPS and gyro
AIS - Automatic Identification System.why: Position, speed and heading are fed automatically from connected sensors.

AIS - Automatic Identification System.q: Which AIS information is entered manually by the crew?
AIS - Automatic Identification System.why: Voyage-related data such as destination, ETA and draught must be updated manually.

AIS - Automatic Identification System.q: Which is a limitation of AIS?
options: It works without any power supply
It shows rocks and unlit buoys automatically
Not all vessels carry AIS or have it switched on
AIS - Automatic Identification System.why: Small craft may not carry AIS and data can be missing or wrong, so it cannot be relied on alone.

AIS - Automatic Identification System.q: How should AIS information be used for collision avoidance?
options: As the only source for decisions
Only when the ship is in port
As an aid, cross-checked with radar and visual lookout
AIS - Automatic Identification System.why: AIS is an aid; COLREGs decisions must be based on all available means including radar and lookout.

AIS - Automatic Identification System.q: Under SOLAS Chapter V, AIS is required on all passenger ships and on ships on international voyages of what size?
AIS - Automatic Identification System.why: SOLAS V/19 requires AIS on ships of 300 GT and upwards on international voyages and all passenger ships.

AIS - Automatic Identification System.q: When may AIS be switched off?
options: When the Master believes it would compromise safety or security
Whenever the ship is in port
AIS - Automatic Identification System.why: IMO guidance says AIS stays on at all times unless the Master judges it a security risk, such as piracy areas.
The MMSI is the nine-digit number identifying a ship's radio station, including its AIS.

AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.q: Why must a centrifugal pump usually be primed before starting?
options: It cannot normally lift liquid when filled with air
It needs oil in the casing to start
It is designed to pump gases only
AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.why: Centrifugal pumps lose suction when air-bound, so the casing must be filled with liquid.

AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.q: What happens if a positive displacement pump runs against a closed discharge valve?
options: Pressure rises dangerously, so a relief valve is needed
AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.why: Positive displacement pumps keep delivering liquid, so pressure builds until something gives way.

AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.q: What is the purpose of a fuel oil purifier?
options: To remove water and solid impurities from the oil
AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.why: Purifiers use centrifugal force to separate water and sludge from fuel or lube oil.

AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.q: What is the difference between a purifier and a clarifier?
options: A purifier only heats the oil
They are exactly the same machine
A purifier removes water and solids; a clarifier mainly removes solids
AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.why: A purifier separates two liquids plus solids, while a clarifier is set up to remove solids.

AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.q: What is the purpose of the intercooler on a multi-stage air compressor?
options: To heat the air before engine starting
To cool the air between stages and improve efficiency
AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.why: Cooling between stages reduces work needed and keeps air temperatures safe.

AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.q: Why are air receivers drained regularly?
options: To remove collected water and oil
AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.why: Water and oil in receivers cause corrosion and can create a fire or explosion risk.

AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.q: What is the function of a lube oil cooler?
options: To heat the fuel oil for burning
To remove heat from the lubricating oil using cooling water
To separate water from the bilge
To raise the oil temperature for starting
AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.why: The cooler keeps lube oil at the right temperature so it lubricates properly.

AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.q: What is the purpose of a boiler safety valve?
options: To release steam if pressure exceeds the set limit
AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.why: The safety valve protects the boiler from overpressure.

AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.q: What is the danger of a very low water level in a boiler?
options: Tubes can overheat and be damaged
AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.why: Without enough water, heated surfaces overheat and can fail.

AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.q: What must be done before maintenance on a pump?
options: Open the casing while under pressure
Keep it running to check vibration
Isolate, lock out and tag out the power and valves
AMMS - Auxiliary Marine Machinery System.why: Isolation and lockout/tagout prevent unexpected start-up or release of pressure.

APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.q: Which IMO code sets ship and port facility security requirements?
APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.why: The International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code covers maritime security.

APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.q: How many security levels are there under the ISPS Code?
What does the Ship Security Alert System (SSAS) do?
options: Sounds a loud alarm on deck
Sends a silent alert to shore authorities
APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.why: SSAS sends a covert alert ashore without warning the attackers onboard.

APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.q: Who is responsible onboard for implementing the Ship Security Plan?
APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.why: The SSO, under the Master, implements and maintains the Ship Security Plan.

APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.q: Which is a recommended ship protection measure in Best Management Practices (BMP)?
options: Physical barriers such as razor wire
Keeping only one lookout at night
APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.why: BMP advises hardening the ship with barriers, extra lookouts and a citadel.

options: A secure area where the crew can shelter with communications
APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.why: A citadel is a protected refuge with supplies and communications for the crew during an attack.

APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.q: What does access control onboard mean?
options: Checking identity and controlling who boards the ship
Locking the galley only at night
APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.why: Access control prevents unauthorized persons from boarding.

APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.q: If pirates board and take control, what should the crew do?
options: Stay calm, cooperate and avoid actions that risk lives
Fight the attackers with any weapons
APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.why: Resistance after boarding puts lives at risk; safety of the crew comes first.

APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.q: Which watchkeeping practice helps detect pirates early?
options: Reducing the bridge team at night
Extra lookouts with binoculars plus radar watch
APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.why: Early detection gives more time to raise alarms and take evasive action.

APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.q: How must the Ship Security Plan be kept?
options: Onboard and protected from unauthorized access
APA - Anti Piracy Awareness.why: The approved SSP is confidential and must be protected onboard.

ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.why: CPA is the closest distance a target will pass if both ships keep course and speed.

options: Time to the closest point of approach
ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.why: TCPA tells how much time remains until the CPA is reached.

ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.q: What does an ARPA trial maneuver show?
options: A recording of the voyage data
The predicted effect of a planned course or speed change
ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.why: Trial maneuver simulates a planned action so its effect on CPA can be checked before acting.

ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.q: Relative vectors are mainly used to:
options: Quickly see if a target is on a collision course
Show the target's course over ground
ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.why: If a target's relative vector points at own ship, there is a risk of collision.

ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.q: Why wait a few minutes after acquiring a target before relying on its data?
options: ARPA needs time to track and calculate a steady course and speed
The target must reply by VHF first
The radar must warm up again
The gyro must be reset each time
ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.why: ARPA calculations become accurate only after several minutes of steady tracking.

ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.q: What happens if wrong gyro or speed log data is fed into ARPA?
options: There is no effect at all
The calculated target data will be wrong
ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.why: ARPA computes true target motion from own heading and speed, so bad inputs give bad results.

options: When ARPA wrongly transfers tracking to a nearby target
When a target sends AIS data
When the radar changes range scale
ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.why: Target swap happens when two echoes pass close and the tracker jumps to the wrong one.

ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.q: Which COLREG rule requires proper use of radar, including radar plotting, to determine risk of collision?
ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.why: Rule 7(b) requires proper use of radar including long-range scanning and radar plotting.

ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.q: For collision avoidance, ARPA true vectors should normally be:
options: Sea-stabilized, to show the target's heading through the water
Ground-stabilized, to show the tidal set
ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.why: Sea-stabilized vectors show the target's aspect, which relates to the COLREGs situation.

ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.q: Which is a limitation of ARPA?
options: It can see behind large obstructions
Small targets in sea or rain clutter may not be tracked
ARPA - Automatic Radar Plotting Aids.why: Weak echoes in clutter may be lost, so a visual and radar lookout must continue.

BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.q: What is the Islamic holy month of fasting called?
BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.why: Ramadan is the month when Muslims fast during daylight hours.
The fast runs from dawn until sunset each day.

BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.q: Which day is the weekly congregational prayer day in Islam?
BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.why: Friday (Jumu'ah) is the day of congregational prayer.

BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.q: Which food is forbidden for Muslims?

BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.why: Halal means allowed; haram means forbidden.

BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.q: Which hand should be used to eat or to give and receive things in Arab culture?
BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.why: The left hand is traditionally considered unclean, so the right hand is used.

BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.q: What does the greeting As-salamu alaykum mean?
BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.why: It is the common Arabic greeting; the reply is Wa alaykum as-salam.

BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.q: How should you behave when Muslim crew members are praying?
options: Avoid walking in front of them and keep noise low
BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.why: Respecting prayer time supports good relations in a multicultural crew.

BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.q: In Arab ports during Ramadan, non-Muslims should:
options: Avoid eating, drinking or smoking in public during fasting hours
Eat openly in front of officials
BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.why: Many Arab countries expect, and some require, no public eating or drinking during fasting hours.

BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.q: What is good professional etiquette when meeting Arab officials?
options: Dress modestly and greet politely, following their lead
Use first names and jokes right away
Sit with the soles of your shoes showing
BAC - Basic Arabic Culture.why: Modest dress and respectful greetings show professionalism; showing shoe soles is considered rude.

BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.q: What does Behavior Based Safety focus on?
options: Observing and improving work behaviors to prevent accidents
BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.why: BBS uses observation and feedback to increase safe behavior and reduce at-risk behavior.

BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.q: Which is an example of at-risk behavior?
options: Wearing a hard hat on deck
Working aloft without a safety harness
BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.why: Working at height without fall protection is a clear at-risk behavior.

BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.q: How should a safety observation be done?
options: Non-punitive and focused on the behavior, not the person
BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.why: BBS works when crew trust that observations are for learning, not punishment.

options: Praising safe behavior so it is repeated
BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.why: Recognizing safe behavior makes it more likely to continue.
Clear, prompt and respectful feedback helps people change behavior.

BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.q: What does the safety pyramid idea teach?
options: Accidents happen only to new crew
Many unsafe acts and near misses happen before a serious accident
Serious accidents have no warning signs
BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.why: Reducing unsafe acts and near misses reduces the chance of serious accidents.

options: Any crew member may stop a job they believe is unsafe
Only shore staff may stop work
Work cannot stop once it starts
Only the Master may stop work
BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.why: Everyone has the right and duty to stop unsafe work without fear of blame.

BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.q: What does the ISM Code require the company to establish?
options: A safety management system with safe work practices
BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.why: The ISM Code requires a documented Safety Management System.

BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.q: In the ABC model of behavior, what do the letters stand for?
BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.why: Antecedents trigger behavior, and consequences make it more or less likely to be repeated.

options: Overconfidence that makes a person less careful in routine tasks
BBSC - Behavioral Based Safety Course.why: Complacency in familiar jobs is a common cause of accidents.

BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.q: What should be done before bunkering starts?
options: Hold a pre-bunkering meeting and complete the checklist
BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.why: The checklist confirms communication, transfer rate, tanks and emergency stop with the supplier.

BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.q: At what standard reference temperature is bunker fuel density normally reported?
BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.why: Fuel density is reported at 15°C so quantities can be compared on the same basis.

BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.q: To convert corrected volume (m³) to mass (metric tonnes), you multiply by:
BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.why: Mass = volume at 15°C x density at 15°C.

options: The distance from the liquid surface to the top reference point
The depth of liquid from the tank bottom
The weight of fuel in the tank
BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.why: Ullage measures empty space from the top; sounding measures liquid depth from the bottom.

BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.q: What is the Volume Correction Factor (VCF) used for?
options: Converting observed volume to volume at 15°C
BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.why: Oil expands when warm, so the VCF corrects observed volume to the standard temperature.

BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.q: Why should bunker tanks not be filled to 100%?
options: To allow for thermal expansion and avoid overflow
Because sounding pipes cannot reach the top
BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.why: Space must be left for expansion and to prevent overflow and spills.

BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.q: Why are deck scuppers plugged during bunkering?
options: To stop any spilled oil from going overboard
BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.why: Plugged scuppers contain spills on deck and prevent pollution.

BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.q: Under MARPOL Annex VI, how long must the Bunker Delivery Note be kept onboard?
BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.why: MARPOL Annex VI Regulation 18 requires the BDN to be retained onboard for three years.

BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.q: Which MARPOL Annex covers fuel oil sulfur limits and the bunker delivery note?
BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.why: Annex VI deals with air pollution, including fuel oil quality and sulfur content.

BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.q: Where must bunkering of fuel oil be recorded under MARPOL Annex I?
BCAF - Bunkering Calculation and Familia.why: Bunkering of fuel or bulk lube oil is an Oil Record Book Part I entry.

BMT - Banksman Training.q: What is the role of a banksman?
options: To guide the crane operator with signals and keep the lift area safe
BMT - Banksman Training.why: The banksman directs the operator when the load or area cannot be seen clearly.

BMT - Banksman Training.q: Who should give lifting signals to the crane operator?
options: Two people at the same time
Whoever is closest to the load
BMT - Banksman Training.why: One signaler avoids confusing or conflicting instructions.

Connect all systems to one open network

Team members question unclear actions and the leader responds

BRM-BTM - Bridge Resources Management wi.q: What is the purpose of a pre-departure bridge briefing?

BRM-BTM - Bridge Resources Management wi.why: A briefing creates a shared understanding before the passage starts.

BRM-BTM - Bridge Resources Management wi.q: How should a passage be monitored?

Fix the position regularly using more than one method

BRM-BTM - Bridge Resources Management wi.q: What leadership style is usually needed in an emergency?

BRM-BTM - Bridge Resources Management wi.q: What is the purpose of a debriefing after a passage or event?

All team members understand the plan and situation the same way

Lift to full height at once
Lift slightly and check the balance and security of the load

Washing jets can create static electricity that may ignite flammable gas

COW - Crude Oil Washing System.q: What should be done if a leak is found in the COW lines?

COW - Crude Oil Washing System.q: What should be done before starting COW?
options: Complete the checklist and test the system for leaks
COW - Crude Oil Washing System.why: Checks confirm the equipment, inert gas and communication are ready and safe.

COW - Crude Oil Washing System.q: Which COW stage washes the lowest parts of the tank to remove sediment?

Fix it yourself by deleting files

Using two passwords written on paper

CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.why: TEU is the standard unit for container capacity, based on a 20-foot container.

CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.q: What does the bay-row-tier system identify?
options: The container's position along, across and up the ship

options: Locking containers to each other and to the deck or hatch
CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.why: Twistlocks fit into corner castings to secure containers in place.

CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.q: How should container lashings be maintained at sea?
options: Check regularly and tighten as needed, especially before bad weather
Check only at the discharge port
CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.why: Lashings can loosen as the ship moves, so they must be checked and tightened.

CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.q: How are heavy containers generally stowed?
CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.why: Heavy containers low in the stack keep the stack stable and the ship's center of gravity low.

CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.q: How is segregation of dangerous goods containers decided?
options: By the IMDG Code segregation requirements
CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.why: The IMDG Code sets how far apart incompatible dangerous goods must be stowed.

CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.q: How should reefer containers be monitored?
options: Open the doors to check the cargo
Check and record the set point and actual temperature regularly
CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.why: Regular checks catch power or unit failures before the cargo spoils.

CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.q: Under SOLAS, what does VGM mean for a packed container?
CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.why: SOLAS requires the shipper to provide the verified gross mass before loading.

CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.q: Parametric rolling is a danger for container ships mainly in:
CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.why: Parametric rolling can build up quickly in head or following seas and cause container losses.

CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.q: What is a key safety rule when working on a container ship deck?
options: Work alone at night without a radio
Wear PPE and stay clear of lifting areas and moving containers
CSF - Container Ship Familiarization.why: Container operations involve heavy moving loads and working at height.

CST - Crane Safety Training.q: What is the main hazard during crane operations?
options: Too much paint on the crane
Dropped or swinging loads striking people
CST - Crane Safety Training.why: Falling or swinging loads cause the most serious lifting injuries.

CST - Crane Safety Training.q: When should a crane pre-use inspection be done?
options: Before each use or shift, as the manufacturer and SMS require
CST - Crane Safety Training.why: Daily checks find defects before they cause a failure.

CST - Crane Safety Training.q: What should a lifting plan include?
options: Load weight, equipment, rigging, sequence, people and hazards
CST - Crane Safety Training.why: A lifting plan makes sure every part of the lift is thought through.

CST - Crane Safety Training.q: Where should the SWL of a crane be shown?
options: Clearly marked on the crane and in its certificates
CST - Crane Safety Training.why: The SWL must be visible so the operator never exceeds it.

CST - Crane Safety Training.q: What is the purpose of an exclusion zone during lifting?
options: To keep people out of the area where a load could fall or swing
CST - Crane Safety Training.why: Barriers and zones keep people away from the danger area.

CST - Crane Safety Training.q: What should be done if communication fails during a lift?
CST - Crane Safety Training.why: Without clear communication, continuing the lift is unsafe.

CST - Crane Safety Training.q: If the crane loses power with a load suspended, what should be done?
options: Keep the area clear and follow the emergency procedure
Walk under the load to check it
CST - Crane Safety Training.why: Securing the area protects people until the load can be lowered safely.

CST - Crane Safety Training.q: What does a hook safety latch do?
options: Prevents the sling from slipping off the hook
CST - Crane Safety Training.why: The latch keeps slings and lifting gear from coming off the hook.

CST - Crane Safety Training.q: What should be done if a defect is found on a crane?
options: Do not use it and report the defect
CST - Crane Safety Training.why: A defective crane must not be used until repaired and checked.

CST - Crane Safety Training.q: What should be assessed before lifting at sea?
CST - Crane Safety Training.why: Weather and ship motion affect load control and crane limits.

DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.q: What does SWL marked on a deck crane mean?
options: Safe Working Load, the maximum load the crane may lift
Slewing Wind Limit for crane operation
Ship Weight Limit for cargo in the hold
Standard Wire Length fitted on the crane drum
DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.why: SWL is the maximum load the crane is certified to lift in normal service and must never be exceeded.

DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.q: Where should crew never stand during a crane lifting operation?
options: Under or near the path of the suspended load
On the opposite side of the hatch
Behind the signalman at a safe distance
DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.why: A suspended load can fall or swing, so no one may stand beneath it or in its path.

DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.q: Who should normally give signals to the crane operator during a lift?
options: The stevedore foreman from the shore
The officer on the bridge by radio only
Any crew member who can see the load
DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.why: Using one designated signalman avoids confusing or conflicting signals to the operator.

DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.q: What is the main purpose of tag lines attached to a load?
options: To replace the main hoisting wire if it fails
To measure the weight of the load
To increase the lifting capacity of the crane
To control swinging and turning of the load
DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.why: Tag lines let crew guide the load from a safe distance without touching it.

DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.q: What should the crane operator do if strong wind makes the load difficult to control?
options: Remove the tag lines so the load moves freely
Lift faster to finish before the wind increases
Stop lifting and follow the wind limits of the manufacturer
Continue the lift but use a longer sling
DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.why: Wind makes loads swing; operations must stop when manufacturer wind limits are reached.

DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.q: Which wire rope condition means the wire must be taken out of service?
options: Slight dust on the outer strands
A light, even coating of wire rope grease
Kinks, bird-caging or many broken wires
DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.why: Kinks, bird-caging and broken wires seriously reduce rope strength and require discard.

DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.q: What happens to the tension in each sling leg when the angle between the legs increases?
options: The tension in each leg increases
The tension in each leg decreases
DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.why: Wider sling angles increase the force on each leg, so slings can be overloaded even with a light load.

DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.q: What is the purpose of the safety latch on a crane hook?
options: To lock the crane in the stowed position
To measure the angle of the jib
To stop the sling from slipping off the hook
To increase the safe working load of the hook
DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.why: The latch keeps the sling eye or shackle from accidentally coming off the hook.

DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.q: Which check is part of the routine pre-use inspection of a deck crane?
options: Repainting the crane jib and housing
Testing limit switches and emergency stop
Replacing all wire ropes every voyage
DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.why: Limit switches and the emergency stop must work before the crane is used.

DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.q: What should be done before lifting a load whose weight is unknown?
options: Find out or confirm the weight before lifting
Use two cranes without checking the weight
Lift it slowly and see if the crane can hold it
Lift it only during daylight hours
DCST - Deck Crane Safety Training.why: The weight must be known so that the SWL of the crane and lifting gear is not exceeded.

DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.q: What is the main use of a windlass on board?
options: Heaving up and lowering the anchor
DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.why: The windlass handles the anchor cable for anchoring and heaving up.

DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.q: What part of the windlass grips the links of the anchor chain?
DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.why: The gypsy (cable lifter) has pockets shaped to hold the chain links.

DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.q: How does a capstan differ from a winch?
options: A capstan has no motor or brake at all
A capstan is only used for cargo
A capstan turns on a vertical axis
A capstan turns on a horizontal axis
DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.why: A capstan has a vertical drum, while a winch drum is horizontal.

DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.q: What is the snap-back zone during mooring operations?
options: The area where mooring ropes are stored
The area where a parting rope may whip back
The place where the pilot boards
The safe area behind the windlass
DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.why: A parting rope under tension can recoil violently into the snap-back zone and injure or kill crew.

DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.q: Why should crew never stand in the bight of a mooring rope?
options: It reduces the power of the winch
The rope can suddenly tighten and trap them
It makes the rope wear out faster
It blocks the view from the bridge
DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.why: A bight can close suddenly under load and catch a person’s legs or body.

DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.q: When the ship is at sea, what device should hold the anchor chain instead of the windlass brake?
options: The chain stopper or devil’s claw
DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.why: The chain stopper holds the chain at sea so the windlass brake is not left carrying the load.

DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.q: Under SOLAS, when must the steering gear be checked and tested before departure?
options: Only after the ship leaves the pilot station
Only once a month while in port
DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.why: SOLAS Chapter V requires steering gear checks and tests within 12 hours before departure.

DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.q: How often must emergency steering drills be held under SOLAS?
options: Only when the steering gear fails
At least once every three months
DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.why: SOLAS Chapter V requires emergency steering drills at least every three months.

DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.q: What must be done before maintenance work on a deck winch?
options: Isolate the power and lock and tag it out
Run the winch slowly while working on it
DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.why: Isolation with lockout/tagout stops the machine from being started during maintenance.

DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.q: Which is a basic routine maintenance task for deck machinery?
options: Leaving drums wet to reduce friction
Greasing moving parts and checking oil levels
DMA - Deck Machinery Awareness.why: Regular lubrication and oil-level checks keep deck machinery reliable and safe.

ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.q: What chart data must be used for ECDIS to meet chart carriage requirements?

Any electronic chart downloaded from the internet
Scanned paper charts with no updates
Charts drawn by the officer of the watch

ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.q: What is the purpose of the safety contour setting?
options: To show the ship’s maximum speed
To set the brightness of the display
To mark the depth line the ship must not cross
ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.why: The safety contour separates safe water from unsafe water based on the ship’s draft and safety margins.

ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.q: What does the safety depth setting do on ECDIS?
options: It sets the depth of the ship’s anchor
It controls the echo sounder output
It highlights soundings shallower than the set depth

Having more than one route loaded

ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.q: Which horizontal datum does ECDIS use for positions?
ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.why: ECDIS and GNSS positions are referenced to the WGS 84 datum.

ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.q: What should the officer do after planning a route on ECDIS?
options: Turn off all alarms during the passage
Run the route check function and review warnings
Delete the safety settings to save memory
ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.why: The route check finds dangers and safety contour crossings along the planned route.

ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.q: What does the cross-track distance (XTD) limit warn about?
options: The ship going faster than the planned speed
The chart needing a new update
The ship moving too far off the planned route
ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.why: The XTD alarm warns when the ship deviates from the route beyond the set limit.

ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.q: Why should the ECDIS position be checked by other means?
options: It is required only in port
GPS errors or sensor faults can give a wrong position
ECDIS cannot show the ship’s position
Paper charts are always more accurate
ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.why: Over-reliance on a single sensor is dangerous, so positions are cross-checked with radar, visual or other fixes.

options: They never need updates once installed
By applying regular updates from the chart service
By correcting them by hand with a pencil
By re-installing the ECDIS software each voyage
ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.why: ENC updates are issued regularly by the chart provider and must be applied and verified.

ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.q: What is required in case the main ECDIS fails?
options: Using a mobile phone map application
An approved back-up such as a second ECDIS or paper charts
Only the ship’s radar without any charts
ECDIS - Operational Use of Electronic Ch.why: SOLAS requires an adequate back-up arrangement for ECDIS to ensure safe navigation if it fails.

EMS - Environmental Management System.q: Which international standard sets the requirements for an environmental management system?

EMS - Environmental Management System.q: Which is an example of an environmental impact?

EMS - Environmental Management System.q: Who is responsible for setting the environmental policy of a company?
EMS - Environmental Management System.why: ISO 14001 requires top management to establish and commit to the environmental policy.

EMS - Environmental Management System.q: Which IMO convention sets the rules for preventing pollution from ships?
EMS - Environmental Management System.why: MARPOL is the main convention for prevention of pollution from ships.

EMS - Environmental Management System.q: What is the purpose of an internal environmental audit?
options: To replace the flag state survey
To punish crew who make mistakes
To check that the system is working and followed
EMS - Environmental Management System.why: Internal audits verify that the EMS is implemented and effective and find areas to improve.

EMS - Environmental Management System.q: What should happen when a nonconformity is found?
options: Find the cause and take corrective action
Hide it until the next voyage
Only record it in a personal notebook
Ignore it if no one was hurt
EMS - Environmental Management System.why: Corrective action removes the cause of a nonconformity so it does not happen again.

EMS - Environmental Management System.q: Which record must be kept on board to log garbage discharges and incineration?
EMS - Environmental Management System.why: MARPOL Annex V requires a Garbage Record Book for garbage operations.

EMS - Environmental Management System.q: Why should environmental objectives be measurable?
options: So they can be changed every day
So progress can be monitored and checked
So only the master knows them
So they do not need any records
EMS - Environmental Management System.why: Measurable objectives allow the ship to monitor results and show continual improvement.

EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.q: What does a solenoid valve do in an electro-pneumatic system?
options: Compresses the air for the system
Uses an electric coil to move a valve and direct air
Removes water from the air supply
EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.why: Energizing the solenoid coil shifts the valve spool to change the air flow path.

EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.q: What does a 5/2 directional valve mean?
options: Five bar pressure and two outlets
Five seconds delay and two signals
EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.why: The first number is the number of ports and the second is the number of switching positions.

A cylinder with two separate pistons
A cylinder that uses oil and air together
A cylinder returned only by a spring
EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.why: A double-acting cylinder uses compressed air to both extend and retract the piston.

EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.q: What is the purpose of an FRL unit?
options: To freeze, reheat and lower the air
To feed, run and log the compressor
To fill, release and lock the cylinder
To filter, regulate and lubricate the air supply
EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.why: The filter-regulator-lubricator prepares clean air at the correct pressure for the components.

EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.q: Why must moisture be drained from compressed air systems?
options: Water causes corrosion and faulty valve operation
EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.why: Moisture corrodes components and can cause valves and actuators to stick.

EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.q: What does a normally closed (NC) solenoid valve do when the coil is not energized?
options: It stays open and allows flow
It stays closed and blocks flow
It vents all air to the atmosphere
It moves to a middle position
EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.why: An NC valve is closed at rest and opens only when the coil is energized.

EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.q: Which device can tell the control circuit that a cylinder has reached its end position?
options: A limit switch or position sensor
EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.why: Limit switches or sensors (e.g. reed switches) send a position signal to the control circuit.

EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.q: Which instrument is commonly used to check whether a solenoid coil is open-circuited?
options: A multimeter on the resistance setting
A hydrometer in the air receiver
A pressure gauge on the air line
A thermometer on the valve body
EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.why: Measuring coil resistance shows if the winding is open or shorted.

EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.q: What must be done before maintenance on electro-pneumatic equipment?
options: Keep the system running to check movement
Increase the air pressure to test for leaks
Isolate the electrical supply and release the air pressure
Only switch off the lights in the area
EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.why: Both the electrical and stored pneumatic energy must be isolated to prevent sudden movement or shock.

EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.q: What is the main job of the air receiver in a pneumatic system?
options: To store compressed air and smooth pressure changes
EPS - Electro Pneumatic System.why: The air receiver stores air and reduces pressure fluctuations in the system.

ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.q: What is the main goal of Engine Room Resource Management?
options: Reducing the number of engineers on board
Using all people, equipment and information for safe operations
Increasing the speed of the main engine
ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.why: ERM aims to use all available resources effectively to keep engine-room operations safe.

Knowing the cost of spare parts
Knowing what is happening around you and what may happen next
Knowing the names of all crew members
ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.why: Situational awareness means perceiving, understanding and anticipating the condition of the plant.

The receiver repeats the message back to confirm it
Writing every order on the notice board
Talking only by radio in the engine room
ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.why: Repeating back confirms the message was received and understood correctly.

ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.q: What should a junior engineer do if they believe a senior’s action is unsafe?
options: Speak up clearly and give the reason
Do the opposite without telling anyone
Stay silent to respect the senior
Wait until the end of the contract
ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.why: Assertiveness helps break the error chain before an accident happens.

ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.q: Under STCW, what is the minimum rest a seafarer must have in any 24-hour period?
ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.why: STCW requires at least 10 hours of rest in any 24-hour period.

options: The list of alarms in the alarm log
The chain used to lift engine parts
The order of watchkeepers on duty
A series of small mistakes that can lead to an accident
ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.why: Accidents usually result from several linked errors; breaking any link can prevent them.

ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.q: What is the purpose of a briefing before a complex engine-room job?
options: To decide who will take the blame
To fill time before starting work
To make sure everyone knows the plan, roles and risks
ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.why: Briefings share the plan and responsibilities so the team works safely together.

ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.q: Who has overall responsibility for the engine department?
ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.why: The Chief Engineer is responsible for the operation and safety of the engine department.

ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.q: Why is complacency dangerous in the engine room?
options: It makes people miss warning signs and skip checks
ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.why: Complacency reduces attention, so abnormal signs and procedures may be overlooked.

ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.q: What should the relieving engineer do before taking over the watch?
options: Confirm the plant condition and any ongoing work
Take over even if not fully fit
Wait for the bridge to call
Sign the log book without checking
ERRM - Engine Room Resource Management.why: The relieving engineer must be satisfied about the plant status and ongoing operations before accepting the watch.

ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.q: What helps avoid confusion about who does each job in the engine room?
options: Letting everyone do any job they want
Giving all orders to one oiler
ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.why: Clear roles prevent duplicated work and tasks being missed.

options: Working without rest to finish quickly
Giving the hardest tasks to the newest crew
Planning and sharing tasks so no one is overloaded
Reducing the number of tasks to zero
ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.why: Spreading tasks and priorities sensibly keeps the team effective and alert.

ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.q: When many alarms sound at the same time, what should the engineer do first?
options: Identify and deal with the most critical alarm
Restart every machine one by one
Silence all alarms and leave the control room
ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.why: Prioritizing the most dangerous condition protects the ship and the plant.

ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.q: What is the immediate priority after a blackout at sea?
options: Restore power safely, starting with the standby generator
Wait for the next watch to arrive
Restart the main engine at full speed
ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.why: Restoring electrical power restores essential services such as steering and lubrication.

ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.q: Why should the bridge be informed of problems in the engine room?
options: It is needed only for the deck log
The bridge may need to change speed or course for safety
The bridge must repair the engine
The bridge controls all engine alarms
ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.why: The navigating officer needs to know about machinery limits to keep the ship safe.

ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.q: What is a good way to keep the team aware during an abnormal condition?
options: Waiting until the problem is fixed to talk
Keeping information only with the leader
Regular short updates to all involved
ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.why: Frequent updates maintain shared situational awareness in the team.

options: A meeting before the job starts
A review after a job to learn what went well and what to improve
A report sent only to the flag state
ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.why: Debriefings capture lessons learned for future operations.

ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.q: What leadership style is usually best in a sudden emergency?
options: Long group discussion before any action
Direct, clear orders from the leader
ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.why: In emergencies quick, clear direction is needed; consultation suits routine work.

ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.q: What is the effect of fatigue on engine-room teamwork?
options: No effect if the person is experienced
ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.why: Fatigue reduces alertness and judgment, increasing the risk of mistakes.

ERTM - Engine Room Team Management.q: When the engine room is unmanned (UMS), who must respond to alarms?

Any cabin with a locked door
A space with limited openings and poor natural ventilation

ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.q: What is the normal oxygen content of fresh air?
ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.why: Fresh air contains about 20.9% (21%) oxygen; entry requires this normal level.

ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.q: In what order should the atmosphere of an enclosed space normally be tested?
options: Oxygen, then flammable gases, then toxic gases
Toxic gases, then oxygen, then flammable gases
ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.why: Oxygen is tested first because low oxygen affects flammable-gas readings and is an immediate danger.

ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.q: Why should the atmosphere be tested at different levels in the space?
options: Because instruments only work near the floor
Some gases are heavier or lighter than air and collect at different heights
To check the paint on the tank walls
ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.why: Heavier gases like H2S collect low and lighter gases rise, so all levels must be checked.

ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.q: What is the main duty of the standby person at the entrance?
options: Enter the space to help with the work
Sign the permit for the entrants
Leave to get tools when needed
Keep watch, keep communication and raise the alarm
ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.why: The standby person must stay at the entrance, communicate and raise the alarm in an emergency.

ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.q: What should the standby person do if an entrant collapses inside?
options: Raise the alarm and not enter without breathing apparatus and backup
Go in immediately to pull the person out
ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.why: Many deaths are rescuers who enter without protection; the alarm brings a properly equipped rescue team.

ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.q: What document authorizes entry into an enclosed space?
ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.why: An entry permit confirms all checks are done and entry is approved for a limited time.

ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.q: Under SOLAS, how often must enclosed space entry and rescue drills be held?
options: Only when a new crew joins
ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.why: SOLAS Chapter III requires enclosed space entry and rescue drills at least every two months.

ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.q: Why must ventilation continue while people are inside the space?
options: To reduce noise in the space
To dry the paint faster only
To keep a safe atmosphere during the work
ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.why: Continuous ventilation prevents a dangerous atmosphere from building up again.

ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.q: Why is a tank that was filled with inert gas dangerous to enter?
options: It has too little oxygen to breathe
It is always flooded with water
ESE - Enclosed Space Entry.why: Inert gas displaces oxygen, so breathing it can cause unconsciousness and death within moments.

FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.q: How is a FRAMO cargo pump driven?
options: By a long shaft from the engine room
By a hydraulic motor at the pump
FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.why: FRAMO pumps are submerged pumps driven by a hydraulic motor powered from a hydraulic power unit.

FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.q: Where is a FRAMO cargo pump located?
options: In a separate cargo pump room
On the main deck beside the manifold
FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.why: Each tank has its own submerged pump, so no cargo pump room is needed.

FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.q: What separates the cargo from the hydraulic oil in a FRAMO pump?
FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.why: The cofferdam between seals keeps cargo and hydraulic oil apart and collects any leakage.

FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.q: Why is the cofferdam purged regularly?
options: To fill the pump with cargo
FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.why: Purging shows any leakage; cargo or hydraulic oil in the purge indicates a failing seal.

FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.q: If hydraulic oil is found when purging the cofferdam, what does it show?
options: A leak at the cargo seal
A leak at the hydraulic oil seal
FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.why: Hydraulic oil in the cofferdam points to leakage from the hydraulic side seal.

FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.q: How is the speed of a FRAMO pump controlled?
options: By adding water to the cargo
By adjusting the hydraulic oil pressure and flow
FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.why: The pump speed follows the hydraulic pressure supplied to the hydraulic motor.

FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.q: How is the last cargo removed from the pump discharge pipe after stripping?
options: By heating the tank to boil the cargo
By opening the tank bottom plug
By running the pump in reverse at high speed
By purging the riser with air or nitrogen
FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.why: The riser is pressurized with air or nitrogen to push remaining cargo out through the discharge line.

FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.q: Why should a FRAMO pump not run dry for long?
options: It can damage the pump bearings and seals
FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.why: The cargo lubricates and cools parts of the pump; dry running causes damage.

FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.q: What is an important check of the hydraulic system before cargo operations?
options: Hydraulic oil level, pressure and filters
The paint color of the pump stack
FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.why: Correct oil level, pressure and clean filters are essential for reliable pump operation.

FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.q: Before maintenance on a FRAMO pump, what must be done?
options: Isolate and depressurize the hydraulic system
FRAMO - FRAMO Pump.why: Stored hydraulic pressure must be released and the system isolated to prevent injury.

H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.q: What smell is hydrogen sulfide known for at low concentrations?
H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.why: H2S has a strong rotten-egg smell at low concentrations.

H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.q: Why can you not rely on smell to detect H2S?
options: Only trained people can smell it
H2S has no smell at any level
The smell is the same as fresh air
High concentrations quickly deaden the sense of smell
H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.why: H2S paralyzes the sense of smell at higher levels, so a gas detector must be used.

H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.q: Is H2S heavier or lighter than air?
options: Heavier, so it collects in low areas
H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.why: H2S is slightly heavier than air and gathers in low places like tank bottoms and pump rooms.

H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.q: Which cargo is a common source of H2S on ships?
H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.why: Sour crude oils and some petroleum products can release H2S.

H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.q: Which other shipboard source can produce H2S?
H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.why: Decomposing organic matter in sewage systems and bilges can generate H2S.

H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.q: What should you use to detect H2S?
options: A calibrated personal or portable gas detector
H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.why: A calibrated gas detector gives reliable warning of H2S.

H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.q: In which direction should you escape from an H2S release?
options: Upwind or crosswind, away from low areas
Toward the gas source to find the leak
H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.why: Moving upwind and away from low areas reduces exposure to the gas.

H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.q: What must a rescuer wear before helping a person overcome by H2S?
H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.why: Rescuers without SCBA risk becoming victims themselves.

H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.q: What is the first aid for a person exposed to H2S after safe rescue?
options: Give the person food and water
Move to fresh air, give oxygen and CPR if needed
Let them sleep in the same area
H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.why: Fresh air, oxygen and CPR if breathing has stopped are the immediate first aid steps.

H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.q: Besides being toxic, what other hazard does H2S have?
options: It is completely harmless in fire
H2S - Hydrogen Sulfide Awareness.why: H2S is flammable and burns to produce toxic sulfur dioxide.

options: Something with the potential to cause harm
The chance that an accident will happen
HAZID - Hazard Identification.why: A hazard is any source that can cause harm, such as a slippery deck or toxic gas.

options: The combination of likelihood and severity of harm
The name of a safety officer
HAZID - Hazard Identification.why: Risk considers how likely harm is and how bad it would be.

HAZID - Hazard Identification.q: In the hierarchy of controls, which is the most effective measure?
HAZID - Hazard Identification.why: Removing the hazard completely is the most effective control.

HAZID - Hazard Identification.q: In the hierarchy of controls, which is the last line of defense?
HAZID - Hazard Identification.why: PPE only protects the wearer and is used when other controls cannot fully remove the risk.

HAZID - Hazard Identification.q: Which is an example of a human-factor hazard?
HAZID - Hazard Identification.why: Human factors include fatigue, stress and complacency that affect performance.

HAZID - Hazard Identification.q: Which is an example of a chemical hazard?
HAZID - Hazard Identification.why: Chemical hazards include solvents, fuels and other substances that can harm health.

HAZID - Hazard Identification.q: Which document gives information on the hazards of a chemical product?
HAZID - Hazard Identification.why: The SDS gives hazards, handling, PPE and first aid for a chemical.

HAZID - Hazard Identification.q: What does the ISM Code require the company to do about risks?
options: Assess all identified risks and set safeguards
Only record accidents after they happen
Leave risk control to port authorities
HAZID - Hazard Identification.why: The ISM Code requires companies to assess identified risks and establish appropriate safeguards.

options: They show hazards before someone is hurt
Because it is a crime not to
HAZID - Hazard Identification.why: Near-miss reports allow hazards to be corrected before an accident occurs.

HAZID - Hazard Identification.q: When should a hazard identification be reviewed?
options: When the job, equipment or conditions change
Only once when the ship is built
Only when the crew changes nationality
HAZID - Hazard Identification.why: Changes can introduce new hazards, so the assessment must be reviewed.

HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.q: How many classes of dangerous goods are there in the IMDG Code?
HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.why: The IMDG Code divides dangerous goods into 9 classes.

HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.q: Which IMDG class covers flammable liquids?
Which IMDG class covers corrosive substances?
