HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.why: A UN number is a four-digit code assigned to a specific dangerous good or group.

HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.q: Which packing group shows the highest danger?
HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.why: Packing Group I is for substances of great danger; III is for minor danger.

HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.q: Which IMO guide gives emergency procedures for fires and spillages of dangerous goods?
HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.why: The EmS Guide gives fire (F) and spillage (S) emergency schedules for dangerous goods.

HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.q: Which guide is used for first aid after exposure to dangerous goods?
HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.why: MFAG gives medical first aid advice for accidents involving dangerous goods.

HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.q: Which SOLAS chapter covers the carriage of dangerous goods?
HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.why: SOLAS Chapter VII covers carriage of dangerous goods and makes the IMDG Code mandatory.

HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.q: What is the purpose of segregation of dangerous goods?
options: To store all dangerous goods in one place
To keep incompatible goods apart to prevent dangerous reactions
HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.why: Segregation separates goods that could react dangerously if they mix or leak.

HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.q: What document must accompany a dangerous goods shipment from the shipper?
HAZMAT - Dangerous, Hazardous and Harmfu.why: The shipper must provide a dangerous goods declaration with the proper shipping name, UN number and class.

HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.q: Which U.S. agency issues the hazardous materials regulations in 49 CFR?
options: PHMSA of the Department of Transportation
HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.why: The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) of DOT issues 49 CFR hazmat rules.

HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.q: Which part of 49 CFR contains the Hazardous Materials Table?
HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.why: The Hazardous Materials Table is in 49 CFR 172.101.

HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.q: Which part of 49 CFR covers carriage of hazardous materials by vessel?
HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.why: Part 176 applies to carriage by vessel.

HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.q: Under 49 CFR, how often must hazmat employees receive recurrent training?
options: At least once every three years
HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.why: 49 CFR 172.704 requires recurrent hazmat training at least once every three years.

HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.q: What must shipping papers under 49 CFR include for emergencies?
HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.why: Shipping papers must show a monitored emergency response telephone number.

HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.q: Can shipments prepared under the IMDG Code be accepted in the U.S.?
options: No, the IMDG Code is never accepted
Yes, 49 CFR allows the IMDG Code under certain conditions
HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.why: 49 CFR permits IMDG Code shipments with the conditions stated in Part 171.

options: A small label on an inner package
A large hazard sign shown on containers and vehicles
HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.why: Placards are large diamond signs showing the hazard class on cargo transport units and vehicles.

HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.q: How many hazard classes do the U.S. hazmat regulations use?
options: 9, the same as the UN system
HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.why: 49 CFR uses the same nine hazard classes as the UN and IMDG systems.

HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.q: What is the main purpose of marking and labeling hazmat packages?
options: To show the price of the goods
To show the contents and hazards to handlers and responders
HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.why: Marks and labels quickly communicate the identity and hazard of the contents.

HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.q: Who is responsible for correctly classifying a hazardous material before shipment?
HAZMAT-CFR - HAZMAT with CFR.why: The shipper must classify, package, mark, label and document the hazmat correctly.

HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.q: What is the main purpose of hatch covers?
options: To keep the cargo holds weathertight
HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.why: Hatch covers close the hold openings and keep seawater out of the cargo.

HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.q: What part presses against the compression bar to make a weathertight seal?
HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.why: The rubber packing is compressed against the compression bar to form the seal.

HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.q: What is the purpose of cleats on hatch covers?
options: To lift the cover off the coaming
To hold the cover down and compress the packing
To drain water from the hold
HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.why: Cleats secure the cover and keep the packing pressed onto the compression bar.

HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.q: Which test is the preferred method to check hatch cover weathertightness?
HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.why: Ultrasonic testing accurately finds leak points with the covers closed and is widely preferred.

HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.q: What does a chalk test check?
options: The strength of the hatch steel
The amount of water in the hold
The speed of the hydraulic system
Contact between the packing and the compression bar
HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.why: Chalk on the compression bar shows where the rubber packing makes contact.

HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.q: What should be done with rubber packing that has a permanent compression set?
options: Grease it and keep using it
HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.why: Permanently compressed packing cannot seal properly and must be renewed.

HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.q: Why should rubber packing never be painted?
options: Paint makes the rubber too soft
Paint hardens the rubber and spoils the seal
HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.why: Painted rubber loses its elasticity and will not seal correctly.

HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.q: What is the purpose of drain channels and non-return valves on hatch covers?
options: To cool the hatch cover in hot weather
To carry away water that passes the outer seal
To pump cargo out of the hold
To fill the hold with ballast water
HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.why: Drain channels lead leaked water away, and non-return valves stop seawater from coming back in.

HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.q: Which defect should be looked for on compression bars during inspection?
HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.why: Damaged or corroded compression bars stop the packing from sealing.

HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.q: What routine maintenance helps rolling hatch covers move smoothly?
options: Cleaning and greasing wheels and rails
HCIM - Hatch Cover Inspection and Mainte.why: Clean, lubricated wheels and rails prevent jamming and uneven seating.

options: Air always flows from low to high pressure
Pressure on a confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions
Heat always rises in a liquid
HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.why: Pascal’s law is the basic principle of hydraulic systems.

HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.q: What is the main difference between hydraulic and pneumatic systems?
options: Hydraulics use air, pneumatics use oil
Hydraulics use liquid, pneumatics use compressed air
HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.why: Hydraulic oil is nearly incompressible while air is compressible.

HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.q: What does a relief valve do in a hydraulic system?
options: Protects the system from too much pressure
HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.why: The relief valve opens to limit maximum pressure and prevent damage.

HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.q: What converts mechanical power into hydraulic power?
HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.why: The pump takes mechanical energy from a motor and creates hydraulic flow.

HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.q: What kind of movement does a hydraulic cylinder produce?
HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.why: Cylinders produce linear motion; hydraulic motors produce rotation.

HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.q: What is the most common cause of hydraulic system failures?
options: Too much paint on the pipes
HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.why: Dirt and water in the oil wear components and block valves.

HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.q: How should you check for a suspected high-pressure hydraulic leak?
options: Look closely with your face near the hose
Run your hand along the hose
Use a piece of cardboard, never your hand
HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.why: High-pressure oil jets can inject oil into the skin, causing serious injury.

HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.q: What does a flow control valve mainly control?
HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.why: Controlling the flow rate controls how fast a cylinder or motor moves.

HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.q: Why must an accumulator be discharged before maintenance?
options: It can store pressure even when the pump is stopped
It makes the oil too cold
It weighs too much to lift
It is needed to start the pump
HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.why: Accumulators hold stored energy that can cause sudden movement or oil release.

HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.q: What must be done before opening any hydraulic or pneumatic line for repair?
options: Increase pressure to test the line
Loosen fittings quickly to drain oil
Isolate the system and release all pressure
HPT - Hydraulic and Pneumatic Training.why: Safe isolation and depressurizing prevents injuries from stored energy.

HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.q: What is the chemical formula for hydrogen sulfide?
HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.why: Hydrogen sulfide is made of two hydrogen atoms and one sulfur atom: H2S.

HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.q: What color is hydrogen sulfide gas?
HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.why: H2S is colorless, so it cannot be seen.

HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.q: How does H2S mainly enter the body?
HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.why: Inhalation is the main route of H2S exposure.

HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.q: Which is an early sign of H2S exposure?
HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.why: Low exposures irritate the eyes and airways and cause headache and nausea.

HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.q: What can happen at very high H2S concentrations?
HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.why: High concentrations can cause rapid unconsciousness, breathing failure and death.

HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.q: What should you do when your personal H2S monitor alarms?
options: Wait for the alarm to stop on its own
Go deeper into the work area
Stop work and leave the area at once
Turn off the alarm and continue working
HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.why: An alarm means a dangerous level is present; leave immediately and report.

HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.q: What is a bump test of a gas detector?
options: Dropping the detector to test its case
A quick check that the detector responds to gas
HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.why: A bump test briefly exposes the sensor to gas to confirm it responds and alarms.

HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.q: What is the purpose of a safe-work boundary around an H2S risk area?
options: To show the route to the galley
To mark where to store food
HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.why: Barriers and signs keep people without monitors or protection away from the hazard.

HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.q: What gas is produced when H2S burns?
HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.why: Burning H2S produces sulfur dioxide, which is also toxic.

HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.q: Before entering a space where H2S may be present, what must be done?
options: Test the atmosphere and obtain a permit
Only open the door and enter
Sniff the air at the entrance
Enter quickly and hold your breath
HSBAT - Hydrogen Sulfide Basic Awareness.why: Gas testing and a permit-to-work confirm the space is safe before entry.

HVT - High Voltage Training.q: On ships, what voltage is generally considered high voltage?
HVT - High Voltage Training.why: Shipboard high voltage generally means systems above 1 kV, such as 3.3 kV, 6.6 kV or 11 kV.

HVT - High Voltage Training.q: Why do large ships use high-voltage systems?
options: Lower current for the same power allows smaller cables
High voltage is completely safe to touch
It removes the need for circuit breakers
HVT - High Voltage Training.why: Higher voltage reduces current, so cables and switchgear can be smaller and losses lower.

HVT - High Voltage Training.q: What document must be issued before work on HV equipment?
HVT - High Voltage Training.why: HV work must be controlled by a formal permit-to-work system.

HVT - High Voltage Training.q: After isolating HV equipment, what must be done before applying earth?
options: Test that it is dead with an approved tester
Touch the conductor with a dry hand
HVT - High Voltage Training.why: Equipment must be proven dead before earthing and starting work.

HVT - High Voltage Training.q: Why are HV conductors earthed (grounded) after isolation?
options: To make the equipment run faster
To discharge stored energy and protect against accidental re-energizing
HVT - High Voltage Training.why: Earthing removes residual charge and protects workers if the circuit is accidentally energized.

HVT - High Voltage Training.q: What is the purpose of lockout and tagout?
options: To prevent equipment from being switched on during work
HVT - High Voltage Training.why: Locks and tags keep isolation devices in the safe position until work is finished.

HVT - High Voltage Training.q: How should a voltage tester be checked when proving equipment dead?
options: Use it only once a year
Check that the battery cover is closed
Test it on a known live source before and after use
Shake it to check it works
HVT - High Voltage Training.why: Proving the tester before and after confirms it worked during the test.

options: A dangerous electrical explosion with intense heat and light
A normal light on a switchboard
HVT - High Voltage Training.why: Arc flash can cause severe burns and injuries, so PPE and safe procedures are essential.

HVT - High Voltage Training.q: What is the first action when finding a person in contact with a live electrical conductor?
options: Pull them away with your bare hands
Wait for them to let go
Switch off the power before touching them
HVT - High Voltage Training.why: Touching a person in contact with live parts can electrocute the rescuer too.

HVT - High Voltage Training.q: What test is commonly done to check the condition of HV cable insulation?
HVT - High Voltage Training.why: Insulation resistance testing shows whether insulation is in good condition.

IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.q: What is the main purpose of the Inventory of Hazardous Materials?
options: To list the cargo carried on each voyage
To list spare parts for the engine
To record the crew’s medical history
To list hazardous materials on board for safe handling and recycling
IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.why: The IHM identifies the location and amount of hazardous materials to protect people and the environment.

IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.q: Which convention requires the Inventory of Hazardous Materials?
options: The Hong Kong International Convention for ship recycling
IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.why: The Hong Kong Convention requires ships to carry and maintain an IHM.

IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.q: What does Part I of the IHM cover?
options: Hazardous materials in the ship’s structure and equipment
IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.why: Part I lists hazardous materials built into the structure and equipment.

IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.q: Which material is commonly listed in the IHM because of health risks?
IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.why: Asbestos is a hazardous material that must be identified and controlled.

IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.q: Which document from suppliers shows if a delivered item contains hazardous materials?
IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.why: Suppliers provide Material Declarations (with a Supplier’s Declaration of Conformity) used to update the IHM.

IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.q: When should the IHM be updated?
options: Only when the ship is sold for scrap
Whenever new equipment or materials are installed or removed
Only when the ship is built
IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.why: The IHM must be kept up to date throughout the ship’s life.

IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.q: When are Parts II and III of the IHM prepared?
options: Before the ship goes for recycling
IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.why: Parts II (wastes) and III (stores) are added before the ship is recycled.

IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.q: Which substance used in old anti-fouling paints is controlled under the IHM?
IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.why: Organotin compounds such as TBT are prohibited hazardous materials listed in the IHM.

IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.q: What should crew do if suspected asbestos material is damaged?
options: Cut it out with a grinder
Stop work, avoid disturbing it and report it
Sweep it up with a broom
IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.why: Damaged asbestos releases dangerous fibers, so it must be left alone and reported for proper handling.

IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.q: Which certificate shows that a ship has an approved IHM?
options: International Certificate on Inventory of Hazardous Materials
IHM - Inventory of Hazardous Materials.why: The International Certificate on IHM is issued after survey of the IHM.

ILO - Basic Arabic Course.q: What is the common Arabic greeting that means "Peace be upon you"?
ILO - Basic Arabic Course.why: As-salamu alaykum is the common Arabic greeting meaning peace be upon you.

ILO - Basic Arabic Course.q: What is the correct reply to "As-salamu alaykum"?

Ma’a salama means goodbye (go with peace).

ILO - Basic Arabic Course.q: In which direction is Arabic written?
ILO - Basic Arabic Course.why: Arabic script is written and read from right to left.

ILO - Basic Arabic Course.q: Which hand is customary to use when eating or giving items to Arabic-speaking persons?

ILO - Basic Arabic Course.q: During Ramadan, what do many Muslims do between dawn and sunset?
options: They fast from food and drink
ILO - Basic Arabic Course.why: Fasting from dawn to sunset is observed during Ramadan, so it is respectful not to eat in front of those fasting where possible.

ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.q: Why must food handlers wash their hands often?
options: To remove germs that can contaminate food
ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.why: Hands carry bacteria that easily transfer to food.

ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.q: For how long should hands be washed with soap and water?
ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.why: Washing for at least 20 seconds with soap removes most germs.

ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.q: What is the temperature "danger zone" where bacteria grow fastest?
ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.why: Bacteria multiply quickly between about 5°C and 60°C, so food should be kept out of this range.

options: Moving harmful bacteria from one food or surface to another
ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.why: Cross-contamination happens when germs pass from raw food, hands or surfaces to other food.

ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.q: How should raw meat be stored in a refrigerator?
options: On the bottom shelf below ready-to-eat food
On the top shelf above cooked food
ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.why: Storing raw meat at the bottom stops juices dripping onto ready-to-eat food.

ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.q: At what temperature should a refrigerator be kept?
ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.why: Chilled food should be kept at 5°C or below to slow bacterial growth.

ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.q: What should a food handler do if they have diarrhea or vomiting?
options: Continue working but wash hands more
Report it and stay away from food handling
Work in the store room instead
ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.why: Sick food handlers can spread infection and must not handle food until cleared.

ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.q: How should a cut on a food handler’s hand be covered?
options: With a waterproof, brightly colored dressing
ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.why: A waterproof, colored plaster keeps germs in and is easy to see if it falls into food.

ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.q: Why should separate cutting boards be used for raw and cooked food?
ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.why: Separate boards stop bacteria from raw food reaching cooked or ready-to-eat food.

ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.q: What is the best way to thaw frozen meat safely?

ILO - Basic Food Hygiene.why: Thawing in the refrigerator keeps the food out of the danger zone.

ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.q: Which nutrient is the body’s main source of energy?
ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.why: Carbohydrates such as rice, bread and potatoes are the main energy source.

ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.q: What is the main role of protein in the diet?
ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.why: Protein from meat, fish, eggs and beans builds and repairs muscles and tissues.

ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.q: Which disease was common among sailors who lacked vitamin C?
ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.why: Lack of vitamin C causes scurvy; fruits and vegetables prevent it.

options: It gives the most energy per gram
It helps digestion and prevents constipation
ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.why: Fiber from vegetables, fruits and whole grains supports healthy digestion.

ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.q: Too much salt in the diet is linked to which health problem?
ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.why: High salt intake raises blood pressure and the risk of heart disease.

Hygiene Assessment for Clean Cooking Practice
Hazard Alert and Cooking Check Points
ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.why: HACCP is a preventive food safety system based on hazard analysis and critical control points.

ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.q: What is the first principle of HACCP?
ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.why: HACCP starts by identifying hazards that could make food unsafe.

ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.q: What is a critical control point (CCP)?

A step where control is essential to prevent or reduce a food hazard
The point where the menu is written
ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.why: A CCP is a step where a hazard can be prevented, eliminated or reduced to a safe level.

ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.q: What is a critical limit in HACCP?
options: The maximum number of meals per day
The value that must be met at a CCP, such as a minimum cooking temperature
ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.why: A critical limit separates safe from unsafe, for example a required core temperature.

ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.q: What makes a balanced meal for seafarers?
options: A variety of foods from all food groups in the right amounts
ILO - Basic Nutrition with HACCP.why: Variety and correct portions provide all the nutrients needed for health and work.

ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.q: What is the purpose of a cycle menu on board?
options: To reduce the number of meals
To plan varied meals over a set period
To serve the same meal every day
ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.why: A cycle menu repeats after a set period and helps plan variety, nutrition and purchasing.

ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.q: What does FIFO mean in stock rotation?
ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.why: FIFO means older stock is used first to reduce spoilage.

ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.q: What should be checked when receiving provisions on board?
options: Only the weight of the truck
Only the color of the boxes
Quantity, quality, temperature and expiry dates
ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.why: Checking deliveries ensures only safe, correct and complete goods are accepted.

ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.q: At what temperature should frozen food be stored?
ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.why: Frozen food is stored at -18°C or colder to keep it safe and in good quality.

ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.q: What should be done with canned food that is swollen or bulging?
ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.why: Bulging cans may contain dangerous bacteria such as Clostridium botulinum.

options: Cooking as much food as possible
Serving food only once a day
Serving a standard amount of food for each person
ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.why: Standard portions control costs, reduce waste and ensure fair servings.

ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.q: Under the MLC 2006, who pays for the food provided to seafarers on board?
options: It is provided free of charge to the seafarer
ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.why: MLC 2006 requires food to be provided free of charge during the period of engagement.

ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.q: Under the MLC 2006, what should food on board take into account?
options: Nutrition, quality, variety and the crew’s religious and cultural practices
ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.why: MLC 2006 requires suitable food in quantity, nutritional value, quality and variety, considering cultural and religious needs.

ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.q: How should dry provisions be stored?
options: In a cool, dry, clean store off the floor
ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.why: Dry, cool and clean conditions off the floor prevent spoilage and pests.

ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.q: Why should hot food be served quickly after cooking?
options: To keep it out of the temperature danger zone
To reduce the number of plates
ILO - Basic Shipboard Food Management.why: Keeping hot food hot prevents bacteria from growing before service.

ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.q: What should you use to put out a fire in a deep-fat fryer?
options: A wet towel thrown from far away
A fire blanket or wet chemical extinguisher
ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.why: Water on burning oil causes a violent flare-up; smother it or use wet chemical agent.

ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.q: What is the first action when a cooking oil fire starts?
options: Turn off the heat source if safe
Open all doors to give it air
ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.why: Shutting off the heat stops the fire from growing; never move a burning pan.

ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.q: How should a knife be carried in the galley?
options: Point down, held close to the side
ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.why: Carrying knives point down reduces the risk of cutting others.

ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.q: What should you do if a knife falls?
options: Step back and let it fall
ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.why: Trying to catch a falling knife often causes serious cuts.

ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.q: Why should galley exhaust hood filters be cleaned regularly?
options: To change the color of the hood
Grease build-up can cause a duct fire
ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.why: Grease in hoods and ducts is a common cause of galley fires.

ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.q: What is the main way to prevent slips in the galley?
options: Clean spills immediately and wear non-slip shoes
ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.why: Prompt cleaning and proper footwear prevent slip injuries.

ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.q: What is the correct way to lift a heavy box of provisions?
options: Bend your back and keep your legs straight
Lift it quickly with one hand
Bend your knees and keep your back straight
ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.why: Using leg strength and a straight back protects against back injury.

ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.q: Why must cold rooms have an alarm and an inside door release?
options: So a person cannot be trapped inside
ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.why: Inside releases and alarms let a trapped person get out or call for help.

ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.q: What should be done after any galley injury or near-miss?
options: Report it only if it costs money
Report it so the cause can be corrected
Keep it secret to avoid trouble
ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.why: Reporting allows hazards to be identified and controlled to prevent repeats.

ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.q: What PPE helps protect against burns when handling hot trays?
ILO - Catering Health and Safety Managem.why: Oven gloves protect against burns; wet cloths conduct heat and can cause scalds.

ILO - Catering Management.q: What is a key duty of the chief cook or catering supervisor?
options: Supervising catering staff, food safety and service quality
ILO - Catering Management.why: The catering supervisor leads the team and ensures safe, good-quality meals.

ILO - Catering Management.q: What is the purpose of a standard recipe?
options: To make every dish taste different
To give consistent quality, portions and cost
ILO - Catering Management.why: Standard recipes give the same result each time and help control cost.

options: Managing purchasing, storage and use so meals stay within budget
ILO - Catering Management.why: Cost control balances budget with nutrition and quality.

ILO - Catering Management.q: How often is a physical stock count (inventory) normally carried out on board?
options: At regular intervals, such as monthly
Only once in the ship’s life
ILO - Catering Management.why: Regular stock counts show actual consumption and help detect losses.

ILO - Catering Management.q: What should be included when planning menus for the crew?
options: Nutrition, variety, crew culture and available stock
ILO - Catering Management.why: Good menus meet nutritional and cultural needs while using stock wisely.

ILO - Catering Management.q: Under the MLC 2006, who must make frequent documented inspections of food and water supplies?
options: The master or an officer acting for the master
ILO - Catering Management.why: MLC 2006 requires the master or a designated officer, with a catering crew member, to inspect at frequent documented intervals.

ILO - Catering Management.q: What is the minimum age for a ship’s cook under the MLC 2006?
ILO - Catering Management.why: MLC 2006 sets 18 as the minimum age for a ship’s cook.

ILO - Catering Management.q: What is the purpose of training catering staff regularly?
options: To keep skills and food safety standards high
ILO - Catering Management.why: Training ensures staff follow safe and efficient practices.

ILO - Catering Management.q: What is procurement in catering management?
options: Planning and buying provisions at the right quality and price
ILO - Catering Management.why: Procurement means sourcing and ordering the right supplies in time.

ILO - Catering Management.q: How can crew feedback help catering management?
options: It shows how to improve meals and service
It is not useful at all
ILO - Catering Management.why: Listening to crew helps match meals to their needs and improve satisfaction.

ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.q: How is the quantity of provisions consumed in a period calculated?
options: Opening stock times number of crew
Opening stock plus purchases minus closing stock
ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.why: Consumption equals what was available (opening plus purchases) minus what is left.

ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.q: What is the daily feeding rate (victualling rate)?
options: The number of meals cooked each day
The food cost per person per day
The salary of the cook per day
ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.why: The daily rate divides total food cost by the number of person-days fed.

ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.q: What is a requisition in the galley?
options: A written request to issue items from the store
ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.why: Requisitions control and record what is taken from the stores.

ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.q: Why should food waste be recorded?
options: To find causes and reduce waste and cost
ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.why: Waste records show where food is lost so it can be reduced.

options: The set amount of an item to keep in stock
The number of crew on board
The highest price for an item
ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.why: Par levels guide ordering so stock is neither too high nor too low.

ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.q: Which practice helps reduce over-production of food?
options: Planning quantities based on the number of persons on board
Preparing all food at once in the morning
ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.why: Matching production to headcount avoids leftovers and waste.

ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.q: What is the benefit of using portion standards?
options: Each serving is the same size and cost is predictable
ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.why: Standard portions make consumption and costs easier to control.

ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.q: Which record shows what items were used each day?
options: The daily usage or issue record
ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.why: Usage records track daily consumption for control and budgeting.

ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.q: What should be done if actual consumption is much higher than planned?
options: Investigate the cause, such as waste, losses or portion sizes
Change the records to match the plan
Ignore it until the next port
ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.why: Investigating variances finds problems like waste or theft so they can be corrected.

ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.q: Why is stock rotation (FIFO) part of consumption control?
options: It increases the daily feeding rate
It makes the store look tidy only
It removes the need to count stock
It reduces spoilage and losses of older stock
ILO - Consumption Control Training Cours.why: Using older stock first prevents food expiring before use.

ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.q: What is the difference between cleaning and disinfecting?
options: Cleaning kills all germs; disinfecting removes dirt
Cleaning removes dirt; disinfecting reduces germs to a safe level
Disinfecting is only done once a year
ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.why: Surfaces are first cleaned of dirt and grease, then disinfected to kill germs.

options: Water that is safe to drink
Water used for engine cooling only
ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.why: Potable water is safe for drinking and food preparation.

ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.q: Which is a sign of pests in a food store?
ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.why: Droppings and damaged packaging show rats, mice or insects are present.

ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.q: What is the best way to prevent cockroaches in the galley?
options: Keep areas clean and food covered, and seal gaps
ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.why: Removing food, water and hiding places keeps pests away.

ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.q: Under MARPOL Annex V, what may never be discharged into the sea?
options: Comminuted food waste far from land
ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.why: MARPOL Annex V prohibits discharge of all plastics into the sea.

options: A plan of what to clean, when, how and by whom
ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.why: A cleaning schedule ensures all areas and equipment are cleaned regularly.

ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.q: Why should garbage bins in the galley have lids?
options: To hide the garbage from the master
To keep out pests and prevent contamination
ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.why: Lidded bins reduce odors, pests and contamination.

ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.q: Which item should be sanitized after cutting raw chicken?
ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.why: Equipment that touched raw meat must be cleaned and sanitized to stop cross-contamination.

ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.q: What should food handlers wear to keep food safe?
options: Clean uniform, apron and hair covering
ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.why: Clean protective clothing and hair covers stop dirt and hair falling into food.

ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.q: Why must chemicals be stored away from food?
options: To prevent chemical contamination of food
To make them easier to reach while cooking
ILO - Food Hygiene and Sanitation.why: Keeping chemicals separate prevents accidental poisoning.

ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.q: How many principles does HACCP have?
ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.why: HACCP is based on seven principles, from hazard analysis to record keeping.

ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.q: What is the purpose of monitoring at a critical control point?
options: To check that critical limits are being met
To count the number of plates
ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.why: Monitoring shows whether each CCP is under control.

ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.q: What should happen when monitoring shows a critical limit was not met?
options: Change the record to look correct
ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.why: Corrective action fixes the problem and deals with unsafe food.

ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.q: Which is an example of a critical control point?
options: Cooking chicken to the required core temperature
Writing the menu on the board
ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.why: Cooking to a safe core temperature kills harmful bacteria, so it is a CCP.

ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.q: What tool is used to check the core temperature of cooked food?
ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.why: A probe thermometer measures the temperature at the center of the food.

ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.q: Why must HACCP records be kept?
options: To show that food safety controls are working
ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.why: Records prove the system is followed and help with verification.

options: Cooking the food a second time
Checking that the HACCP system is working effectively
ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.why: Verification confirms that the plan is correct and being followed.

ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.q: What is the purpose of hot holding food at 63°C or above?
options: To stop bacteria from growing before serving
ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.why: Keeping hot food at 63°C or above keeps it out of the danger zone.

ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.q: Which hazard type is a piece of broken glass in food?
ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.why: Foreign objects like glass, metal or hair are physical hazards.

ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.q: Which hazard type is Salmonella bacteria?
ILO - Food Hygiene with HACCP.why: Bacteria, viruses and parasites are biological hazards.

ILO - Food Hygiene.q: When must food handlers wash their hands?
options: Only at the end of the shift
Before handling food and after using the toilet
Only before eating their own meal
ILO - Food Hygiene.why: Hands must be washed before food handling and after toilet use, raw food, or garbage.

ILO - Food Hygiene.why: Foodborne illness comes from food contaminated with germs or toxins.

ILO - Food Hygiene.q: Which food is a common source of Salmonella?
options: Dry rice in a sealed bag
ILO - Food Hygiene.why: Salmonella is often found in raw chicken and eggs.

ILO - Food Hygiene.q: How long should cooked food stay at room temperature before chilling?
options: As short as possible, no more than about 2 hours
ILO - Food Hygiene.why: Cooked food left out allows bacteria to grow; it should be chilled quickly.

ILO - Food Hygiene.q: Why should jewelry not be worn when preparing food?
options: It can hold germs and fall into food
It changes the taste of food
ILO - Food Hygiene.why: Jewelry traps dirt and bacteria and can become a physical hazard in food.

ILO - Food Hygiene.q: What should be done with food that is past its use-by date?
ILO - Food Hygiene.why: Food past its use-by date may be unsafe and should not be served.

ILO - Food Hygiene.q: What is the purpose of disinfecting food contact surfaces?
ILO - Food Hygiene.why: Disinfection reduces bacteria on surfaces that touch food.

ILO - Food Hygiene.q: How should leftover cooked rice be handled?
options: Leave it in the pot overnight
Cool it quickly, refrigerate and use soon
ILO - Food Hygiene.why: Rice left warm can grow Bacillus cereus, which makes toxins.

ILO - Food Hygiene.q: Which bacteria can come from a food handler’s nose, mouth or skin?
ILO - Food Hygiene.why: Staphylococcus aureus is commonly carried on human skin and in the nose.

ILO - Food Hygiene.q: What should be done with dirty cleaning cloths?
options: Use the same cloth all week
Leave them wet on the counter
Use them to dry hands and plates
ILO - Food Hygiene.why: Dirty cloths spread bacteria, so they must be changed and washed regularly.

ILO - Food Safety Training.q: What are the three main types of food hazards?
ILO - Food Safety Training.why: Food hazards are grouped as biological, chemical and physical.

ILO - Food Safety Training.q: Which is an example of a chemical food hazard?
ILO - Food Safety Training.why: Cleaning chemicals, pesticides and similar substances are chemical hazards.

ILO - Food Safety Training.q: Which is an example of a physical food hazard?
ILO - Food Safety Training.why: Foreign objects such as metal, glass or plastic are physical hazards.

ILO - Food Safety Training.q: What is the safest way to store chemicals in the galley area?
options: In labeled containers, away from food
ILO - Food Safety Training.why: Labeled chemicals stored apart from food prevent accidental contamination.

ILO - Food Safety Training.q: What is the purpose of cooking food thoroughly?
ILO - Food Safety Training.why: Proper cooking temperatures destroy most harmful microorganisms.

ILO - Food Safety Training.q: What should you do with food that may have touched broken glass?
options: Pick out the glass and serve it
Serve it only to the crew mess
ILO - Food Safety Training.why: Small glass pieces may not be visible, so the food must be discarded.

ILO - Food Safety Training.q: How should ready-to-eat food be protected during distribution and service?
options: Covered and kept at the correct temperature
ILO - Food Safety Training.why: Covering and temperature control protect food from contamination and bacterial growth.

ILO - Food Safety Training.q: Which virus is often linked to outbreaks of vomiting and diarrhea on ships?
ILO - Food Safety Training.why: Norovirus spreads easily through food, surfaces and people in closed communities like ships.

options: A food substance that causes an allergic reaction in some people
ILO - Food Safety Training.why: Allergens such as peanuts, shellfish and eggs can cause serious reactions in sensitive people.

ILO - Food Safety Training.q: Why should raw and cooked foods be prepared in separate areas?
ILO - Food Safety Training.why: Separation stops bacteria from raw food reaching food that will not be cooked again.

ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.q: Which temperature range is known as the danger zone, where bacteria grow fastest?
ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.why: Bacteria multiply quickly between about 5°C and 60°C, so food should spend as little time as possible in this range.

ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.q: Which of these is a physical food hazard?
ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.why: Physical hazards are foreign objects such as glass, metal or bone that can injure the person eating the food.

ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.q: When chilled food is delivered on board, what should be checked?
options: Temperature, packaging condition and expiry date
The total weight of all deliveries combined
The brand name and country of the supplier
The number of boxes on each pallet only
ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.why: Temperature, packaging and dates show whether the food is still safe to accept.

ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.q: In a refrigerator, where should raw meat be stored?
options: On the top shelf above cooked food
On the bottom shelf below cooked food
On the door shelves for easy access
ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.why: Keeping raw meat at the bottom stops its juices from dripping onto cooked or ready-to-eat food.

ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.q: What is a safe way to thaw frozen meat?
options: Leave it on the galley counter overnight
Thaw it slowly in the refrigerator
Soak it in warm water for several hours
Place it near the hot galley range
ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.why: Thawing in the refrigerator keeps the meat out of the danger zone while it defrosts.

options: Transfer of harmful germs from one food or surface to another
Mixing two different recipes in one pot
Cooking food at two different temperatures
Storing dry food and canned food together
ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.why: Cross-contamination is the spread of bacteria, for example from raw meat to cooked food through hands, boards or knives.

ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.q: Hot food kept ready for service should be held at what temperature?
ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.why: Holding hot food at 60°C or above keeps it out of the danger zone.

ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.q: A food handler has diarrhoea and vomiting. What should he do?
options: Work only in the dry store
Report to his supervisor and stay away from food handling
Take medicine and return to the galley at once
ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.why: Sick food handlers can pass germs to food, so they must report and be kept away from food work until cleared.

ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.q: Which MLC 2006 regulation covers food and catering on board?
ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.why: MLC 2006 Regulation 3.2 sets the requirements for food and catering for seafarers.

ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.q: A chiller is found running too warm. What is the correct corrective action?
options: Ignore it if the food still smells fine
Switch off the chiller to let it rest
Add more food to keep it cold
Check the food, discard unsafe items and report it for repair
ILO - Food Safety and Hygiene.why: Corrective action means removing food that may be unsafe and fixing the cause of the problem.

ILO - Food and Catering Management.q: Under MLC 2006, how must food be provided to seafarers during their engagement?
ILO - Food and Catering Management.why: MLC 2006 Regulation 3.2 requires that seafarers be provided with food free of charge during their engagement.

ILO - Food and Catering Management.q: Which nutrient is the body's main source of energy?
ILO - Food and Catering Management.why: Carbohydrates such as rice, bread and potatoes are the body's main energy source.

ILO - Food and Catering Management.q: What should menu planning on board take into account?
options: Nutrition, crew culture and religious needs
ILO - Food and Catering Management.why: MLC 2006 requires food that is nutritious and suited to the crew's religious requirements and cultural practices.

ILO - Food and Catering Management.q: Which stock rotation method makes sure older items are used first?
ILO - Food and Catering Management.why: FIFO means the oldest stock is used first, which reduces spoilage.

ILO - Food and Catering Management.q: Under MLC 2006, what is the minimum age for a ship's cook?
ILO - Food and Catering Management.why: MLC 2006 Standard A3.2 states that no seafarer under 18 shall work as a ship's cook.

ILO - Food and Catering Management.q: Under MLC 2006, who carries out frequent documented inspections of food and water supplies?
options: The master or an officer under his authority
ILO - Food and Catering Management.why: MLC 2006 requires frequent documented inspections of food, water and catering spaces by or under the authority of the master.

ILO - Food and Catering Management.q: What helps a catering supervisor keep the same portion size every time?
ILO - Food and Catering Management.why: Standard recipes, ladles and scoops give consistent portions and control food cost.

ILO - Food and Catering Management.q: How is food cost per person per day calculated?
options: Total food cost multiplied by the number of crew
Number of crew divided by voyage days
Total stores weight divided by number of meals
Total food cost divided by (number of crew x number of days)
ILO - Food and Catering Management.why: Dividing total food cost by the number of man-days gives the daily cost per person.

ILO - Food and Catering Management.q: Which record shows the food items received and issued from the storerooms?
ILO - Food and Catering Management.why: The provision inventory record tracks what comes in, what is issued and what remains.

ILO - Food and Catering Management.q: A messman is seen not washing hands before handling food. What should the catering supervisor do?
options: Explain the correct practice and follow up
Report it only at the end of the contract
Do the messman's tasks himself every time
ILO - Food and Catering Management.why: A good supervisor corrects unsafe practice at once and checks that it improves.

ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.q: What are the main factors when planning provisions for a voyage?
options: Only the price of each item
Voyage length, number of crew and menu plan
ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.why: Provisions must match how many people will eat, for how long, and what the menu requires.

ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.q: When provisions arrive, what should they be checked against?
ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.why: Comparing the delivery with the order confirms correct items, quantities and quality.

ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.q: A delivery of frozen meat shows signs of thawing and refreezing. What should you do?
options: Reject it and record the reason
Accept it and cook it right away
Refreeze it as quickly as possible
Mix it with the good stock
ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.why: Thawed and refrozen meat may be unsafe, so it should be rejected and the reason documented.

ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.q: How should dry stores be kept?
options: On the floor near the bulkhead
Off the floor in a cool, dry, ventilated room
In the engine room for warmth
ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.why: Dry, cool, ventilated storage off the floor protects food from moisture, pests and spoilage.

ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.q: Why must cleaning chemicals be stored away from food?
options: Because the cook uses them daily
To prevent chemical contamination of food
ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.why: Keeping chemicals separate prevents them from leaking or being mistaken for food.

ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.q: Under FEFO stock rotation, which items are issued first?
options: Items with the earliest expiry date
ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.why: FEFO means First Expired, First Out, so items that expire soonest are used first.

ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.q: What is the usual storage temperature for frozen provisions?
ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.why: Frozen food is normally kept at -18°C or colder to stop bacterial growth and keep quality.

ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.q: Why should a provision inventory be taken regularly?
options: To give the crew extra meals
To know stock levels and plan the next order
To change the menu every day
ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.why: Regular inventory shows what is left, reveals losses and guides the next order.

ILO - Galley (Provision) Management.q: Where should fresh fruits and vegetables be stored?
options: In the same box as raw fish
In the dry store with the flour

MECAR - Medical Care - Refresher.q: What is the Glasgow Coma Scale used to assess?
MECAR - Medical Care - Refresher.why: The Glasgow Coma Scale scores eye, verbal and motor responses to measure consciousness.

MECAR - Medical Care - Refresher.q: What is normal adult body temperature?
Why should the patient's condition and treatment be recorded?
options: For continuity of care and handover to doctors
MECAR - Medical Care - Refresher.why: Good records let others continue treatment and help doctors ashore.

MECAR - Medical Care - Refresher.q: Why is the medical chest inventory checked?
options: To make sure medicines are present, in date and properly stored
MECAR - Medical Care - Refresher.why: Regular checks ensure the right medicines are available and usable when needed.

MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.q: What is the first thing you should do when you reach an injured crew member?
options: Give the casualty water to drink
Check that the area is safe for you and the casualty
Carry the casualty to the ship's hospital at once
Remove the casualty's clothing to look for injuries
MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.why: Checking for danger first prevents the rescuer from becoming a second casualty.

MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.q: In the ABC of casualty assessment, what does the letter 'A' stand for?
MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.why: A stands for Airway, because an open airway is needed before breathing and circulation can be supported.

MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.q: What is the correct ratio of chest compressions to rescue breaths in adult CPR?
MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.why: Current adult basic life support guidelines use 30 compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths.

MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.q: At what rate should chest compressions be given to an adult during CPR?
MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.why: Guidelines recommend 100 to 120 compressions per minute to keep blood flowing to the brain.

MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.q: What is the first action to control severe bleeding from a wound?
options: Apply firm direct pressure on the wound
Give the casualty a warm drink
Leave the wound uncovered to dry
MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.why: Firm direct pressure is the quickest and most effective first step to stop severe bleeding.

MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.q: The recovery position is used for which casualty?
options: A conscious casualty with a sprained ankle
A casualty who is not breathing
An unconscious casualty who is breathing normally
MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.why: The recovery position keeps the airway open and lets fluids drain for an unconscious person who is still breathing.

MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.q: What is the correct first aid for a heat burn on the arm?
options: Apply butter or toothpaste on the burn
Cool the burn with clean, cool running water
Burst the blisters to release the fluid
Cover the burn with cotton wool
MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.why: Cooling with clean running water reduces heat damage and pain without adding infection risk.

MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.q: When the ship needs advice from a doctor ashore, the master should contact:
MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.why: TMAS provides radio or satellite medical advice from qualified doctors to ships at sea.

MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.q: Which signs suggest that a casualty is going into shock?
options: Pale, cold, clammy skin and a rapid, weak pulse
Red, hot, dry skin and a slow pulse
Normal skin colour and a strong, steady pulse
Itchy skin and slow, deep breathing
MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.why: Shock reduces blood flow to the skin, causing pale clammy skin and a fast, weak pulse.

MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.q: A conscious adult is choking and cannot speak, cough or breathe. What should you do?
options: Give water to wash the object down
Give back blows and abdominal thrusts
Lay the casualty flat and wait
MEFAR - Medical First Aid - Refresher.why: Back blows and abdominal thrusts are the standard first aid to clear a blocked airway in a conscious adult.

MHA - Mental Health Awareness.q: Which is a common source of stress for seafarers?
options: Having too many shore leave days
MHA - Mental Health Awareness.why: Long separation from family and home is one of the most common stressors in seafaring life.

MHA - Mental Health Awareness.q: Which behaviour may be an early sign that a crewmate is in psychological distress?
options: Being cheerful and sociable as usual
Withdrawing from others and losing interest in activities
MHA - Mental Health Awareness.why: Withdrawal and loss of interest are common early warning signs of distress or depression.

MHA - Mental Health Awareness.q: A crewmate seems very upset and stressed. What is the best first response?
options: Tell the whole crew so they can watch him
Ignore it because it is a private matter
Talk privately, listen without judging and encourage him to get help
Tell him to stop complaining and work harder
MHA - Mental Health Awareness.why: Private, respectful listening builds trust and helps the person accept support.

MHA - Mental Health Awareness.q: A crewmate says he is thinking of ending his life. What should you do?
options: Keep it a secret as he asked
Wait until the end of the contract
Tell him to sleep it off
Stay with him and report to the master or a senior officer at once
MHA - Mental Health Awareness.why: Talk of suicide is an emergency, so the person must not be left alone and help must be called immediately.

MHA - Mental Health Awareness.q: Which free, confidential, 24-hour helpline is available to seafarers?
MHA - Mental Health Awareness.why: ISWAN's SeafarerHelp offers free, confidential support to seafarers and their families at any time.

MHA - Mental Health Awareness.q: Which habit best helps protect mental wellbeing on board?
options: Skipping rest hours to finish work early
Regular sleep, exercise and contact with family
Drinking alcohol to relax after every watch
Staying alone in the cabin during free time
MHA - Mental Health Awareness.why: Good sleep, physical activity and social connection are proven ways to reduce stress.

MHA - Mental Health Awareness.q: Why is reducing stigma about mental health important on board?
options: It makes seafarers more willing to ask for help early
It removes the need for rest hours
It allows the company to skip medical exams
It means problems no longer need reporting
MHA - Mental Health Awareness.why: When people are not ashamed or afraid, they seek help sooner, before problems become serious.

options: A sudden injury from heavy lifting
A skin condition from sun exposure
Physical and emotional exhaustion from long-term stress
A normal feeling after one long watch
MHA - Mental Health Awareness.why: Burnout is a state of exhaustion caused by prolonged stress that is not managed.

MHA - Mental Health Awareness.q: Under the MLC, 2006, a seafarer who is being harassed on board can:
options: Use the on-board complaint procedure without fear of victimization
Settle it by fighting the other person
Post about it on social media first
MHA - Mental Health Awareness.why: The MLC, 2006 requires on-board complaint procedures and protects seafarers from victimization for using them.

MHA - Mental Health Awareness.q: Which statement shows respectful support to a distressed crewmate?
options: 'Other people have it worse than you.'
'I am here to listen if you want to talk.'
MHA - Mental Health Awareness.why: Offering to listen without judging shows care and encourages the person to open up.

MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.q: Which United Nations agency is responsible for the safety of shipping and prevention of pollution from ships?
MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.why: The IMO is the UN specialized agency that sets global standards for shipping safety, security and pollution prevention.

MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.q: Which convention mainly covers ship construction, fire safety and life-saving appliances?
MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.why: SOLAS, the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea, sets minimum safety standards for ships.

MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.q: What is the main purpose of MARPOL?
MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.why: MARPOL is the main international convention for preventing pollution of the marine environment by ships.

MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.q: What does the STCW Convention set?
options: Standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for seafarers
MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.why: STCW sets minimum standards for seafarer training, certification and watchkeeping.

MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.q: The Maritime Labour Convention, 2006 was adopted by which organization?
options: UN Conference on Trade and Development
MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.why: The MLC, 2006 is an ILO convention that sets seafarers' rights to decent work and living conditions.

MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.q: What is the flag State of a ship?
options: The country where the ship was built
The country of the ship's next port
The country where the ship is registered and whose flag it flies
The country of most of the crew
MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.why: The flag State is the State of registry, which has jurisdiction and control over the ship.

options: Inspection of foreign ships in a nation's ports to check compliance with conventions
Control of port fees by the harbour master
Inspection of local fishing boats only
MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.why: Port State control lets a country inspect foreign ships in its ports to verify they meet international standards.

MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.q: Under UNCLOS, a coastal State's territorial sea may extend up to:
MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.why: UNCLOS allows a territorial sea of up to 12 nautical miles from the baselines.

MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.q: Which Philippine agency is the single maritime administration responsible for implementing the STCW Convention?
MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.why: Republic Act No. 10635 designates MARINA as the single maritime administration for STCW implementation.

MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.q: Which certificate on board shows that the ship operates under a safety management system meeting the ISM Code?
MLA - Maritime Law Awareness.why: The Safety Management Certificate is issued to a ship after verifying its safety management system complies with the ISM Code.

options: Knowing what is happening around you and what may happen next
MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.why: Situational awareness means perceiving what is happening, understanding it and predicting what comes next.

options: The receiver repeats the message back and the sender confirms it
Using the radio only during emergencies
Giving orders without waiting for a reply
MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.why: Repeating back and confirming makes sure the message was heard and understood correctly.

MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.q: What is a common effect of fatigue on a watchkeeper?
MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.why: Fatigue slows reactions and weakens judgement, increasing the risk of errors and accidents.

MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.q: Under STCW, the minimum hours of rest for a watchkeeper are:
options: 6 hours in any 24 hours and 50 hours in any 7 days
8 hours in any 24 hours and 60 hours in any 7 days
12 hours in any 24 hours and 90 hours in any 7 days
10 hours in any 24 hours and 77 hours in any 7 days
MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.why: STCW requires at least 10 hours of rest in any 24-hour period and 77 hours in any 7-day period.

MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.q: Which leadership style is usually most suitable during an emergency?
options: Directive, with clear and quick commands
Waiting until everyone agrees before acting
MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.why: In emergencies there is little time, so clear and direct orders keep the team coordinated.

MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.q: What is a 'just culture' on board?
options: Encouraging reporting of errors and near misses without fear of unfair blame
MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.why: A just culture encourages honest reporting so the ship can learn from mistakes, while still addressing reckless behaviour.

MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.q: A junior officer sees that the senior officer's action may be unsafe. What should he do?
options: Stay silent because the senior knows best
Wait until after the watch to mention it
Speak up clearly and respectfully about the danger
Fix it secretly without telling anyone
MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.why: Assertive, respectful communication can break an error chain before an accident happens.

options: A false sense of safety that comes from routine
MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.why: Complacency is when familiarity with a task makes people less alert to its dangers.

MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.q: What does a good team leader do when giving out work?
options: Assigns tasks according to each person's skills and checks understanding
Blames the team when things go wrong
MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.why: Matching tasks to skills and confirming understanding improves safety and team performance.

MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.q: Studies of marine accidents show that the most common contributing factor is:
MLH - Marine Leadership and Human Behavi.why: Most marine casualties involve human factors such as fatigue, poor communication and wrong decisions.

MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.q: Under the ISM Code, the master has overriding authority to:
options: Make decisions on safety and pollution prevention and request company help
MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.why: The ISM Code gives the master overriding authority and responsibility for safety and pollution prevention decisions.

MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.q: What is the role of the Designated Person Ashore (DPA)?
options: Provide a link between the ship and the company's highest level of management
Inspect the ship for the port State
MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.why: The ISM Code requires a DPA with direct access to top management to support safe operation of the ship.
Annex VI regulates air pollution, including sulphur oxides, nitrogen oxides and ozone-depleting substances.

MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.q: The Garbage Record Book requirement comes from which MARPOL Annex?
MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.why: MARPOL Annex V covers garbage, including the Garbage Management Plan and Garbage Record Book.

MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.q: Records of seafarers' daily hours of rest must be kept on board under:
MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.why: Both STCW and the MLC, 2006 require records of hours of rest to be maintained and available for inspection.

MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.q: Under MARPOL, discharging plastics into the sea is:
options: Allowed beyond 12 nautical miles from land
Allowed if ground into small pieces
MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.why: MARPOL Annex V prohibits the discharge of all plastics into the sea everywhere.

MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.q: A port State control officer may detain a ship when:
options: The crew asks for shore leave
Deficiencies are clearly hazardous to safety, health or the environment
The ship has a newly joined master
MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.why: Detention is used when deficiencies are serious enough to make the ship unsafe to proceed to sea.

MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.q: When an oil pollution incident happens, the officer in charge should:
options: Wait until the next port to report it
Clean it up quietly and make no record
Ask the crew to keep it confidential
Report it without delay following the SOPEP
MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.why: MARPOL requires pollution incidents to be reported without delay, following the Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan.

MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.q: Under the MLC, 2006, the Seafarer Employment Agreement must be:
options: Signed by both the seafarer and the shipowner or representative
MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.why: The MLC requires a signed agreement, with the seafarer keeping a copy, so the terms are clear to both sides.

MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.q: Which document shows that a seafarer is fit for duty at sea?
options: A certificate of proficiency in survival craft
A medical certificate from a recognized doctor
A certificate of competency as officer
MLSO - Maritime Law for Ship Officers.why: STCW and the MLC require a valid medical certificate confirming the seafarer is medically fit for duty.

MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.q: In the hierarchy of controls, which is the most effective way to reduce risk?
MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.why: Removing the hazard completely is always more effective than protecting people from it.

options: An accident that caused serious injury
An event that could have caused harm but did not
MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.why: A near miss is an unplanned event that had the potential to cause injury or damage but did not.

MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.q: Why should near misses be reported?
options: To prevent future accidents by learning from them
MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.why: Near-miss reports reveal hazards so they can be corrected before someone gets hurt.

MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.q: Which is an example of an occupational health hazard in the engine room?
MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.why: Long exposure to high noise can cause permanent hearing loss, which is an occupational health hazard.

MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.q: Before using a chemical on board, which document should you read?
MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.why: The SDS explains the chemical's hazards, safe handling, required PPE and first aid.

MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.q: What is the safe way to lift a heavy load by hand?
options: Bend your back and lift quickly
Keep the load close and lift using your legs
Lift with your arms stretched out
MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.why: Keeping the load close and using the leg muscles reduces strain on the back.

MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.q: What is the purpose of lockout/tagout?
options: To show equipment is ready for use
To prevent equipment from being started while work is done on it
To lock tools away from theft
MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.why: Lockout/tagout isolates energy sources so machinery cannot start accidentally during maintenance.

MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.q: Under the ISM Code, who must establish the safety management system?
MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.why: The ISM Code places the duty to develop and maintain the safety management system on the Company.

MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.q: What is every crew member's safety responsibility on board?
options: Leave safety matters to the officers only
Remove machine guards to work faster
Follow safe work procedures and report hazards
MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.why: Every person on board must work safely and report hazards so they can be controlled.

MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.q: Which practice best prevents slips, trips and falls on deck?
options: Keeping walkways clear and cleaning up spills
Leaving tools on deck after work
MOSHA - Marine Occupational Safety and H.why: Good housekeeping removes the most common causes of slips, trips and falls.

MP - Marine Positioning.q: When fixing the ship's position with two visual bearings, the best angle between the position lines is about:
MP - Marine Positioning.why: Two position lines crossing near 90 degrees give the most accurate fix because small errors have the least effect.

MP - Marine Positioning.q: Why is a fix using three bearings better than one using two?
options: The size of the triangle formed shows if there is an error
It is faster than taking two bearings
It removes the need for a chart
MP - Marine Positioning.why: A third bearing forms a 'cocked hat' whose size shows how reliable the fix is.
GNSS is the general term for satellite positioning systems such as GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou.

MP - Marine Positioning.q: Before plotting a GPS position on a paper chart, the navigator should check that:
options: The chart is printed in colour
The GPS display is set to full brightness
The ship's speed is below 5 knots
The chart datum matches the GPS datum, usually WGS 84
MP - Marine Positioning.why: If the chart datum differs from the GPS datum, the plotted position can be wrong by a significant distance.

MP - Marine Positioning.q: When fixing position by radar, which statement is correct?
options: Radar bearings are more accurate than radar ranges
Radar ranges are generally more accurate than radar bearings
Radar cannot be used for position fixing
Radar ranges are accurate only at night
MP - Marine Positioning.why: Radar measures range very accurately, while bearings are affected by beam width, so ranges give better fixes.

MP - Marine Positioning.q: A dead reckoning (DR) position is found using:
options: Course and distance run from a last known position
MP - Marine Positioning.why: DR applies the course steered and distance run to the last known position.

MP - Marine Positioning.q: What is an advantage of a transit (two charted objects seen in line)?
options: It works well in thick fog
It shows the ship's speed over ground
It gives a position line free from compass error
It replaces the need for a lookout
MP - Marine Positioning.why: A transit is observed by eye, so the position line does not depend on compass accuracy.

MP - Marine Positioning.q: What is good practice for reliable navigation?
options: Check the position using more than one independent method
Fix the position only once a day
MP - Marine Positioning.why: Cross-checking with independent methods detects errors in any single system.

MP - Marine Positioning.q: Which instrument is used to take a visual compass bearing of a landmark?
options: A bearing repeater with an azimuth circle
MP - Marine Positioning.why: An azimuth circle on a gyro repeater or compass is used to measure visual bearings.

MP - Marine Positioning.q: How can the echo sounder help in checking the ship's position?
options: By comparing measured depth with the charted depth
MP - Marine Positioning.why: If the measured depth does not match the chart at the plotted position, the position may be wrong.

MRC - Media Response Course.q: After a maritime incident, who should speak to the media?
options: Any crew member who saw the incident
MRC - Media Response Course.why: One approved spokesperson keeps information accurate, consistent and authorized.

MRC - Media Response Course.q: A reporter asks you, a crew member, about an incident on board. What should you do?
options: Give your personal opinion on the cause
Refuse rudely and push the reporter away
Politely refer the reporter to the company's spokesperson
MRC - Media Response Course.why: Polite referral to the designated spokesperson avoids wrong or unauthorized statements.

MRC - Media Response Course.q: When answering questions from the media, a spokesperson should:
options: Give only confirmed facts and avoid guessing
Guess the cause to satisfy reporters
Blame a crew member right away
MRC - Media Response Course.why: Speculation can spread false information and harm investigations, so only confirmed facts should be given.

MRC - Media Response Course.q: Names of injured or missing crew should be:
options: Released right away to the media
Withheld until the next of kin have been informed
Posted on social media by crewmates
Given to any caller who asks
MRC - Media Response Course.why: Families must hear the news first and privately, not from the media.

MRC - Media Response Course.q: Why is saying 'no comment' usually discouraged?
options: It takes too long to say
It can sound like the company is hiding something
MRC - Media Response Course.why: It is better to explain what can be shared and when, since 'no comment' may suggest a cover-up.

MRC - Media Response Course.q: In crisis communication, the first message should show:
options: Concern for the people affected and actions being taken
MRC - Media Response Course.why: Showing care for people and explaining the response builds trust in the first hours of a crisis.

MRC - Media Response Course.q: A crew member has photos of an incident on board. What should he do with them?
options: Share them quickly so families know
Share them only with close friends
Not post them and follow the company communication policy
Post them but remove the names
MRC - Media Response Course.why: Incident information is confidential and must be released only through the company's approved channels.

MRC - Media Response Course.q: Why must media messages be coordinated with the company's emergency response team?
options: So all statements are consistent and accurate
To delay the news for weeks
MRC - Media Response Course.why: Coordination prevents conflicting statements that can confuse the public and damage credibility.

options: A brief first statement confirming the incident while facts are gathered
A legal contract with the media
A copy of the crew list
MRC - Media Response Course.why: A holding statement acknowledges the incident quickly and promises updates while facts are confirmed.

MRC - Media Response Course.q: When talking with a reporter, you should assume that:
options: Off-the-record remarks will never be printed
Microphones are always off after the interview
Anything you say may be published
MRC - Media Response Course.why: Any remark to a reporter can be quoted, so speak as if everything is on the record.

OPA - Oil Pollution Act.q: Which oil spill led the United States to pass the Oil Pollution Act of 1990?
OPA - Oil Pollution Act.why: The 1989 Exxon Valdez spill in Alaska led directly to OPA 90.

OPA - Oil Pollution Act.q: Under OPA 90, tank vessels operating in U.S. waters must have an approved:
OPA - Oil Pollution Act.why: OPA 90 requires tank vessels to carry a U.S. Coast Guard approved Vessel Response Plan for oil spills.

OPA - Oil Pollution Act.q: Which U.S. agency mainly enforces OPA 90 for vessels at sea?
OPA - Oil Pollution Act.why: The U.S. Coast Guard enforces OPA 90 vessel requirements and leads response to spills at sea.

OPA - Oil Pollution Act.q: OPA 90 introduced a phase-in requirement for tankers in U.S. waters to have:
OPA - Oil Pollution Act.why: OPA 90 required tank vessels trading to the U.S. to be built with or converted to double hulls.

OPA - Oil Pollution Act.q: Under OPA 90, who is the 'responsible party' for an oil spill from a vessel?
options: The owner, operator or demise charterer of the vessel
OPA - Oil Pollution Act.why: OPA 90 makes the owner, operator or demise charterer liable for removal costs and damages.

OPA - Oil Pollution Act.q: Vessels over 300 gross tons in U.S. waters must show proof that they can pay for oil spill costs. This document is the:
OPA - Oil Pollution Act.why: The COFR proves the vessel has financial means to cover OPA 90 liability.

OPA - Oil Pollution Act.q: Under OPA 90 response plans, the 'Qualified Individual' is:
options: A person in the U.S. with authority to start spill response and hire resources
OPA - Oil Pollution Act.why: The Qualified Individual must be in the U.S. with full authority to activate response contractors and spend funds.

OPA - Oil Pollution Act.q: An oil spill into U.S. waters must be reported immediately to:
OPA - Oil Pollution Act.why: U.S. law requires immediate notification of oil discharges to the National Response Center.
