options: Tide and cargo changes alter line tension
SMO - Safe Mooring Operations.why: Changes in draft and tide loosen or overload lines, so they must be adjusted.

SMO - Safe Mooring Operations.q: Why should lines of different materials not be mixed in the same direction?
options: They stretch differently, so one line takes most of the load
SMO - Safe Mooring Operations.why: Lines with different elasticity share load unevenly, which can overload and part the stiffer line.

SMO - Safe Mooring Operations.q: What is the best way to communicate during mooring operations?
options: Clear radio contact with agreed signals and the bridge
SMO - Safe Mooring Operations.why: Clear, agreed communication between stations and the bridge prevents misunderstandings.

SMO - Safe Mooring Operations.q: What should be checked on mooring lines before use?
SMO - Safe Mooring Operations.why: Worn or damaged lines can part under load and must be identified before use.

SMO - Safe Mooring Operations.q: Which PPE is required for mooring operations?
SMO - Safe Mooring Operations.why: Helmets, gloves and safety shoes protect against impact, rope burns and crushing.

SMO - Safe Mooring Operations.q: What type of stopper should be used on a synthetic fibre mooring line?
options: A fibre rope stopper of suitable material
SMO - Safe Mooring Operations.why: Fibre lines need a compatible fibre stopper; chain stoppers are used for wire ropes.

SNC - Safe Navigation Course.q: What does the frequency of position fixing mainly depend on?
options: The ship's distance from navigational dangers
The number of crew on watch
SNC - Safe Navigation Course.why: The closer the ship is to danger, the more often its position must be fixed.

SNC - Safe Navigation Course.q: Under COLREG Rule 6, which factor helps decide safe speed?
options: The arrival time requested by the agent
SNC - Safe Navigation Course.why: Visibility, traffic density and manoeuvrability are key factors in safe speed.

SNC - Safe Navigation Course.q: On which frequency are international NAVTEX navigational warnings broadcast?
SNC - Safe Navigation Course.why: International NAVTEX broadcasts in English on 518 kHz.

SNC - Safe Navigation Course.q: What is the purpose of parallel indexing on radar?
options: To monitor the ship's cross-track distance from a fixed object
To measure the depth of water
To count the number of targets
SNC - Safe Navigation Course.why: Parallel indexing gives a continuous check of the ship's position relative to its planned track.

options: The error caused by the ship's own magnetism
The difference between gyro and radar bearings
The change in compass reading with speed
The angle between true north and magnetic north
SNC - Safe Navigation Course.why: Variation is caused by the earth's magnetic field; deviation is caused by the ship's own magnetism.

SNC - Safe Navigation Course.q: Why should GPS positions be cross-checked with other methods?
options: GPS can have errors or lose signal without warning
GPS is not allowed at night
SNC - Safe Navigation Course.why: Relying on one system is risky; radar and visual fixes confirm the GPS position.

SNC - Safe Navigation Course.q: When should the officer of the watch NOT hand over the watch?
options: While a manoeuvre or avoiding action is in progress
SNC - Safe Navigation Course.why: STCW guidance says handover should wait until the manoeuvre or avoiding action is completed.

SNC - Safe Navigation Course.q: Three position lines form a small triangle (a cocked hat). Which position should be used?
SNC - Safe Navigation Course.why: Taking the position nearest danger gives the safest assumption.

SNC - Safe Navigation Course.q: What is a dead reckoning position?
options: A position from a GPS receiver
A position from three radar ranges
A position worked out from course and speed only
A position given by the pilot
SNC - Safe Navigation Course.why: Dead reckoning uses course steered and speed run, without allowing for current or wind.

SNC - Safe Navigation Course.q: When should the officer of the watch call the master?
options: When in doubt or as stated in the master's standing orders
SNC - Safe Navigation Course.why: The OOW must call the master whenever in doubt or in situations listed in standing orders.

SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.q: Under COLREG Rule 5, how must a proper lookout be kept?
options: By sight, hearing and all available means
SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.why: Rule 5 requires lookout by sight and hearing and all available means appropriate to the conditions.

SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.q: How can an officer tell that risk of collision exists?
options: The other ship shows a red light
The compass bearing of the other ship does not change appreciably
The other ship is sounding its horn
SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.why: Rule 7 states that a steady compass bearing with closing range indicates risk of collision.

SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.q: Two power-driven vessels meet head-on. What should each do?
SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.why: Rule 14 requires each vessel to alter course to starboard so they pass port to port.

SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.q: In a crossing situation between two power-driven vessels, which one must keep out of the way?
options: The one that has the other on her own starboard side
SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.why: Rule 15 says the vessel with the other on her starboard side is the give-way vessel.

SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.q: A vessel is overtaking when it approaches another from more than how many degrees abaft her beam?
SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.why: Rule 13 defines overtaking as coming up from more than 22.5 degrees abaft the beam.

SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.q: In restricted visibility, what sound signal does a power-driven vessel making way give?
options: One prolonged blast at intervals of not more than 2 minutes
SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.why: Rule 35 requires one prolonged blast at least every 2 minutes for a power-driven vessel making way.

SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.q: What does one short blast on the whistle mean when vessels are in sight of each other?
options: I am altering my course to port
I am altering my course to starboard
I do not understand your intentions
SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.why: Rule 34 states one short blast means I am altering my course to starboard.

SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.q: According to Rule 8, how should action to avoid collision be taken?
options: Positive, in ample time and large enough to be readily seen
Slowly, using many small course changes
Only after the other ship acts
SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.why: Rule 8 requires early, substantial action that is readily apparent to the other vessel.

SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.q: Which is a known limitation of radar?
options: It shows the name of every ship
Small targets may be lost in sea or rain clutter
SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.why: Sea and rain clutter can hide small craft, so radar must be used carefully.

SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.q: Why should AIS information not be used alone for collision avoidance?
options: Not all vessels carry AIS and its data may be wrong
AIS is not shown on the bridge
SNCA - Safe Navigation and Collision Avo.why: Some vessels have no AIS and data can be incorrect, so radar and visual checks are still needed.

SNT - Safe Navigation Training.q: What does a cross-track distance (XTD) alarm on ECDIS warn about?
options: The ship moving too far off its planned track
SNT - Safe Navigation Training.why: The XTD alarm warns when the ship goes beyond the set limit from the planned route.

SNT - Safe Navigation Training.q: Which is a good way to cross-check the GPS position?
options: Radar range and bearing of a fixed charted object
Look at the ship's speed log only
SNT - Safe Navigation Training.why: A radar fix on a charted object independently confirms the GPS position.

SNT - Safe Navigation Training.q: How can the gyro compass error be checked at sea?
options: By taking a bearing of a celestial body or a transit
By comparing with the speed log
By asking another ship on VHF
SNT - Safe Navigation Training.why: Azimuths, amplitudes or transit bearings give a known true bearing to compare with the gyro.

SNT - Safe Navigation Training.q: What is closed-loop communication on the bridge?
options: Writing all orders in the log
The receiver repeats the order and the sender confirms it
SNT - Safe Navigation Training.why: Repeating back orders and confirming them prevents misunderstandings.

SNT - Safe Navigation Training.q: Which ECDIS setting helps prevent grounding?
SNT - Safe Navigation Training.why: The safety contour highlights water too shallow for the ship's draft.

SNT - Safe Navigation Training.q: When a pilot is on board, what is the master and OOW's responsibility?
options: They may leave the bridge freely
The pilot takes full legal responsibility
They remain responsible for the safety of the ship
SNT - Safe Navigation Training.why: The presence of a pilot does not relieve the master or OOW of their duties.

SNT - Safe Navigation Training.q: What is the purpose of the Bridge Navigational Watch Alarm System (BNWAS)?
options: To detect fire on the bridge
To monitor the alertness of the officer of the watch
SNT - Safe Navigation Training.why: BNWAS raises an alarm if the OOW does not respond, for example if asleep or incapacitated.

SNT - Safe Navigation Training.q: Why is the echo sounder important for safe navigation?
SNT - Safe Navigation Training.why: The echo sounder shows depth under the keel and warns of shoaling water.

SNT - Safe Navigation Training.q: For a radar fix, which is usually more accurate?
SNT - Safe Navigation Training.why: Radar ranges are generally more accurate than radar bearings.

SNT - Safe Navigation Training.q: What is the main danger of relying on a single navigation system?
options: It makes the bridge too quiet
Errors or failure may go unnoticed
SNT - Safe Navigation Training.why: Without cross-checks, a faulty system can lead the ship into danger unnoticed.

SOC - Safety Officer Course.q: What is the purpose of a permit-to-work system?
options: To control high-risk work through formal checks and approval
SOC - Safety Officer Course.why: A permit to work ensures hazards are identified and controlled before high-risk work starts.

SOC - Safety Officer Course.q: In the hierarchy of controls, which is the most effective?
SOC - Safety Officer Course.why: Removing the hazard completely is the most effective control; PPE is the last resort.

SOC - Safety Officer Course.q: In risk assessment, risk is usually measured by combining which two factors?
SOC - Safety Officer Course.why: Risk is assessed from how likely an event is and how serious its consequences would be.

SOC - Safety Officer Course.q: Why should near misses be reported?
options: To learn and prevent future accidents
SOC - Safety Officer Course.why: Near-miss reports reveal hazards so they can be fixed before someone is hurt.

options: A short meeting before work to discuss hazards and controls
SOC - Safety Officer Course.why: Toolbox talks brief the team on the task, hazards and precautions before starting.

SOC - Safety Officer Course.q: Under the ILO MLC, a ship's safety committee is required on ships with how many seafarers or more?
SOC - Safety Officer Course.why: MLC Standard A4.3 requires a ship's safety committee on ships with five or more seafarers.

SOC - Safety Officer Course.q: What is the main goal of a shipboard safety inspection?
options: To identify hazards and arrange corrective action
To check the ship's paint colour
SOC - Safety Officer Course.why: Inspections find unsafe conditions so they can be corrected and followed up.

SOC - Safety Officer Course.q: Which is an example of an unsafe act?
SOC - Safety Officer Course.why: An unsafe act is something a person does; the others are unsafe conditions.

SOC - Safety Officer Course.q: Under the ISM Code, how should hazardous situations and non-conformities be handled?
options: Ignored if no one was hurt
SOC - Safety Officer Course.why: The ISM Code requires reporting and analysis of non-conformities and hazardous occurrences.

SOC - Safety Officer Course.q: What is usually discussed at a shipboard safety meeting?
SOC - Safety Officer Course.why: Safety meetings review incidents and hazards and agree on improvements.

SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.q: Under MARPOL Annex I, which ships must carry a SOPEP?
options: Oil tankers of 150 GT and above and other ships of 400 GT and above
Only ships trading internationally above 10,000 GT
SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.why: MARPOL Annex I requires a SOPEP on oil tankers of 150 GT and above and other ships of 400 GT and above.
The SOPEP must be approved by the Administration of the flag State.

SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.q: What is the first action when an oil spill is discovered on deck during bunkering?
options: Raise the alarm and stop the transfer
Wash the oil overboard with water
SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.why: Stopping the source and raising the alarm limits the spill and starts the response.

SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.q: Why are deck scuppers plugged before bunkering?
options: To stop spilled oil from going overboard
SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.why: Plugged scuppers keep any spill on deck where it can be contained and cleaned.

SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.q: Which record book is used to record oil operations in the machinery spaces?
options: The Oil Record Book Part I
SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.why: Oil Record Book Part I records machinery space operations such as bunkering and sludge disposal.

SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.q: Which item is commonly found in the SOPEP locker?
SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.why: SOPEP equipment includes absorbents, scoops, shovels and containers for spill clean-up.

SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.q: When an oil pollution incident happens, who must be informed without delay?
SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.why: MARPOL and the SOPEP require prompt reporting to the nearest coastal State.

SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.q: What information does the SOPEP contain?
options: Reporting procedures, contacts and steps to control a discharge
SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.why: The SOPEP lists who to contact and what actions to take to control oil discharge.

SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.q: Why are SOPEP drills carried out regularly?
options: So the crew knows their duties and can respond quickly
SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.why: Regular drills make sure crew can respond quickly and correctly to a spill.

SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.q: Before using chemical dispersants on a spill at sea, what is needed?
options: Nothing, they may be used freely
Approval from the coastal State authority
SOPEP - Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergenc.why: Dispersants can harm marine life, so coastal State approval is normally required.

SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.q: The ISPS Code is part of which SOLAS chapter?
SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.why: The ISPS Code is made mandatory through SOLAS Chapter XI-2.

SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.q: What does security level 1 mean under the ISPS Code?
options: Normal level with minimum security measures at all times
Heightened risk for a period of time
A security incident is likely or imminent
SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.why: Level 1 is the normal level where minimum protective measures are always maintained.

SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.q: Who on board is responsible for implementing the Ship Security Plan?
SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.why: The SSO, accountable to the master, implements and maintains the Ship Security Plan.

SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.q: Who approves the Ship Security Plan?
options: The flag Administration or an authorised organisation
SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.why: The SSP is approved by the flag Administration or a recognised security organisation on its behalf.

SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.q: What is a key access control measure at the gangway?
options: Checking ID and logging all persons boarding
Letting visitors in if they look official
Leaving the gangway unattended at night
Allowing anyone with a parcel on board
SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.why: Checking identity and logging visitors prevents unauthorised access.

SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.q: Why should security patrols be done at irregular times and routes?
options: To make patrols easier to schedule
To avoid predictable patterns that intruders could exploit
SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.why: Unpredictable patrols make it harder for intruders to avoid detection.

SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.q: What is a Declaration of Security (DoS)?
options: An agreement on security measures between a ship and a port facility or another ship
SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.why: A DoS records the security responsibilities agreed between the ship and the other party.

SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.q: What is special about the Ship Security Alert System (SSAS)?
options: It sounds a loud alarm on deck
It sends a covert alert to shore without alarming the ship
SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.why: The SSAS sends a silent alert to shore so attackers on board are not warned.

options: A security incident is probable or imminent
SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.why: Level 3 applies when a security incident is probable or imminent and exceptional measures are needed.

SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.q: You find a suspicious unattended package on board. What should you do?
options: Do not touch it, keep people away and report it
Open it to check the contents
Move it to the store room
SOTC - Security Officer Training Course.why: Suspicious items should be isolated and reported, not handled.

SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.q: What is the main purpose of a workplace inspection on board?
options: To find hazards before they cause accidents
SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.why: Regular inspections identify hazards early so they can be controlled.

SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.q: What is the difference between a hazard and a risk?
options: They mean exactly the same thing
A risk is always a fire
A hazard can cause harm; risk is the chance and severity of that harm
SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.why: A hazard is the source of harm, while risk combines its likelihood and consequence.

SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.q: What is the purpose of root cause analysis after an accident?
options: To find the underlying reasons so it does not happen again
SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.why: Root cause analysis looks beyond the immediate cause to prevent recurrence.

SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.q: After corrective action is taken, what should the safety officer do?
options: Verify that the action was effective
Repeat the same action every day
Ask the crew to forget the incident
SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.why: Follow-up confirms that the corrective action actually removed or reduced the hazard.

SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.q: What does a blue circular safety sign usually mean?
options: A mandatory action, such as wearing PPE
SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.why: Blue circular signs show mandatory actions, such as wearing ear or eye protection.

SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.q: What oxygen level in an enclosed space is considered normal and safe for entry?
SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.why: Normal air contains about 21 percent oxygen; lower or higher levels are dangerous.

SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.q: Why is good housekeeping important for safety?
options: It reduces slips, trips and fire hazards
It makes the ship look expensive
SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.why: Clean, tidy work areas prevent many common accidents and fire risks.

SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.q: What is the role of a fire watch during hot work?
options: To watch for fire and be ready with extinguishing equipment
SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.why: The fire watch monitors for sparks and fire and responds immediately.

SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.q: How can the safety officer help new crew members work safely?
options: Give a proper safety familiarisation and training
Let them learn by trial and error
Assign them the most dangerous jobs first
Skip training if they have experience
SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.why: Familiarisation and training make sure new crew know hazards, procedures and emergency duties.

SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.q: What does the accident pyramid idea teach?
options: Serious accidents happen without warning signs
Many near misses and unsafe acts come before a serious accident
SSOC - Shipboard Safety Officer Course.why: Reducing near misses and unsafe acts lowers the chance of a serious accident.

SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.q: What is the purpose of a Ship Security Assessment?
options: To identify threats and weaknesses as the basis for the security plan
SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.why: The SSA identifies threats and vulnerabilities and forms the basis of the Ship Security Plan.

SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.q: How should the Ship Security Plan be kept on board?
options: Posted on the notice board for all visitors
Protected from unauthorised access or disclosure
SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.why: The SSP is confidential and must be protected from unauthorised access.

SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.q: Under ISPS guidance, how often should security drills be conducted on board?
options: At least once every three months
SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.why: ISPS Code Part B recommends security drills at least once every three months.

SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.q: Who normally sets the security level for a ship?
SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.why: The flag State's Contracting Government sets the security level that applies to its ships.

SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.q: Which behaviour could be a sign of a security threat?
options: A pilot boarding at the scheduled time
A stevedore wearing a proper ID
A person photographing the ship's security arrangements
SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.why: Unusual interest in security arrangements may indicate surveillance by a potential attacker.

SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.q: Before the ship leaves port, what search helps prevent stowaways?
options: A thorough search of the ship's spaces
A check of the fuel tanks only
A test of the general alarm only
SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.why: Searching the ship before departure helps detect stowaways hiding on board.

SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.q: Which STCW Code section sets the competence standard for Ship Security Officers?
SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.why: STCW Code Section A-VI/5 covers the training and competence of Ship Security Officers.

SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.q: To whom should the SSO report security incidents?
options: The master and the Company Security Officer
SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.why: Security incidents are reported to the master and CSO, who inform authorities as required.

SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.q: Why does the SSO carry out internal reviews of security activities?
options: To check the plan is working and correct weaknesses
SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.why: Regular reviews confirm the security measures are effective and up to date.

SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.q: What is the main purpose of a security exercise compared with a drill?
options: It is only a paperwork check
It tests wider coordination, often with the company and authorities
It is done only by the master alone
SSOR - Ship's Security Officer - Refresh.why: Exercises test communication and coordination among ship, company and port or government parties.

options: Ocean Cargo Inspection and Management Forum
Official Classification for International Maritime Fleets
SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.why: OCIMF is the Oil Companies International Marine Forum, which runs the SIRE programme.
SIRE is OCIMF's Ship Inspection Report Programme for tankers and other vessels.

SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.q: What does the inspector use as the guide for questions during a SIRE inspection?
SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.why: Inspectors follow the OCIMF Vessel Inspection Questionnaire during SIRE inspections.

SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.q: Who decides whether a tanker is acceptable for a charter after a SIRE inspection?
options: The SIRE inspector on the spot
The charterer or oil company using the report
SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.why: SIRE reports have no pass or fail; each charterer makes its own vetting decision.
TMSA is OCIMF's tool for companies to assess and improve their management systems.

SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.q: During a vetting inspection, the inspector asks a rating about the emergency shutdown procedure. What is expected?
options: Refer every question to the master
Give a long speech about another topic
Explain or show the procedure correctly
SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.why: Inspections check crew readiness, so crew must know and demonstrate their duties.

SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.q: SIRE 2.0 places greater focus on what area?
options: Human factors and how crew actually perform tasks
The age of the ship's furniture
SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.why: SIRE 2.0 places strong emphasis on human factors and observed crew performance.

SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.q: Why must records such as rest hours be accurate before a vetting inspection?
options: Records are only for the crew's use
Inspectors compare records with real practice and check for consistency
Accurate records slow down the inspection
SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.why: Inconsistent or false records are serious observations and damage the ship's credibility.

SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.q: How should the operator handle observations from a SIRE report?
options: Ignore them because there is no pass or fail
Argue with the inspector on board
Investigate root causes and record corrective and preventive actions
SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.why: Good corrective-action management fixes the cause and shows charterers the issue is closed.

SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.q: Which safety systems are commonly checked during a tanker vetting inspection?
options: Inert gas, fire-fighting and cargo safety systems
SVI - SIRE and Vetting Inspection.why: Inspectors check critical tanker safety systems such as inert gas and fire-fighting equipment.

TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.q: What are the three sides of the fire triangle?
TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.why: A fire needs fuel, oxygen and heat; removing one puts it out.

TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.q: What is the flash point of a liquid?
options: The lowest temperature at which it gives off enough vapour to ignite briefly
The temperature at which it freezes
The temperature at which it boils
The highest temperature it can be stored at
TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.why: Flash point is the lowest temperature at which vapour can momentarily ignite with a flame.

TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.q: Under SOLAS, cargo tanks protected by inert gas must keep oxygen content at or below what level?
TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.why: SOLAS requires inerted cargo tank atmospheres to have no more than 8 percent oxygen by volume.

TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.q: How is the risk from static electricity reduced during cargo transfer?
options: By loading at maximum rate from the start
By bonding, earthing and slow initial loading rates
By spraying water on the manifold
TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.why: Bonding and slow initial rates reduce static build-up and discharge.

TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.q: Why is hydrogen sulphide (H2S) especially dangerous?
options: It is always visible as a yellow cloud
It can quickly deaden the sense of smell and is toxic
TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.why: H2S smells of rotten eggs at low levels but paralyses smell at higher levels and is highly toxic.

TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.q: What is the flammable range of a vapour?
options: The concentration between the lower and upper flammable limits
Any concentration below the lower flammable limit
Any temperature above the boiling point
The distance a flame can travel
TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.why: Only mixtures between the lower and upper flammable limits can burn.

TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.q: Which document gives information on a cargo's hazards and handling?
TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.why: The SDS lists the cargo's properties, hazards, PPE and first aid.

options: The International Safety Guide for Oil Tankers and Terminals
TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.why: ISGOTT is the main industry safety guide for oil tanker and terminal operations.

TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.q: What must be completed between the ship and terminal before cargo transfer?
TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.why: The ship/shore safety checklist confirms both sides have agreed safety measures.

TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.q: Before entering a cargo pump room, what must be done?
options: Ventilate it and test the atmosphere
TANKFAM - Tanker Familiarization and Saf.why: Pump rooms can collect toxic or flammable gas, so ventilation and gas testing come first.

options: The weight of water the ship displaces, equal to the ship's weight
The height of the ship above water
TAS - Trim and Stability.why: A floating ship displaces water equal to its own total weight (Archimedes' principle).

options: The difference between the forward and aft drafts
TAS - Trim and Stability.why: Trim is the difference between forward and aft drafts.

TAS - Trim and Stability.q: What is the centre of buoyancy (B)?
options: The geometric centre of the underwater volume
The centre of the ship's weight
TAS - Trim and Stability.why: B is the centre of the underwater volume, where the buoyant force acts.
GM equals the height of the metacentre (KM) minus the height of the centre of gravity (KG).

TAS - Trim and Stability.q: What is the effect of slack tanks (free surface effect) on stability?
options: It lowers the centre of gravity
TAS - Trim and Stability.why: Free surface effect causes a virtual rise of G, which reduces the effective GM.

TAS - Trim and Stability.q: Loading a heavy weight high on deck will usually do what?
TAS - Trim and Stability.why: Adding weight high raises the centre of gravity, reducing GM.

TAS - Trim and Stability.q: A ship with a very large GM is called stiff. How does it roll?
options: It does not roll at all
TAS - Trim and Stability.why: A large GM gives a short, jerky roll that can damage cargo and tire the crew.

TAS - Trim and Stability.q: A ship is trimmed by the stern when what is true?
options: The aft draft is greater than the forward draft
The forward draft is greater than the aft draft
The ship is listing to starboard
TAS - Trim and Stability.why: Trim by the stern means the stern is deeper than the bow.

TAS - Trim and Stability.q: What is the centre of gravity (G)?
options: The point through which the total weight of the ship acts
The highest point of the ship
TAS - Trim and Stability.why: G is the point where the whole weight of the ship is considered to act downward.

TAS - Trim and Stability.q: What do the load line (Plimsoll) marks show?
options: The position of the cargo holds
The maximum draft the ship may safely load to
TAS - Trim and Stability.why: Load line marks show the deepest allowed draft for different seasons and waters.

TI - Tank Inspection.q: Before entering a tank for inspection, what must be done first?
options: Ventilate, test the atmosphere and obtain an entry permit
Enter quickly before the gas builds up
Enter with a lit match to test for gas
Close all openings to keep it clean
TI - Tank Inspection.why: Enclosed spaces may lack oxygen or contain toxic or flammable gas, so ventilation, testing and a permit come first.

TI - Tank Inspection.q: What is the normal oxygen level in safe air?
TI - Tank Inspection.why: Normal air has about 21 percent oxygen, which is required for safe entry.

TI - Tank Inspection.q: Why should the tank atmosphere be tested at different levels?
options: Gas detectors only work at the top
It is a paperwork rule only
Gases can collect at different heights
TI - Tank Inspection.why: Heavier and lighter gases collect at different levels, so testing must cover the whole space.

TI - Tank Inspection.q: What is the duty of the standby person at the tank entrance?
options: Enter the tank to help with the inspection
Keep contact with the entrants and raise the alarm if needed
Leave once the team is inside
TI - Tank Inspection.why: The standby person monitors the team and calls for help but does not enter alone.

TI - Tank Inspection.q: Which is an example of coating breakdown?
options: Blistering and rust spots on the surface
TI - Tank Inspection.why: Blistering, flaking and rust show that the protective coating is failing.

TI - Tank Inspection.q: Which of these is a structural defect to look for in a tank?
TI - Tank Inspection.why: Cracks, buckling and heavy wastage weaken the structure and must be reported.

TI - Tank Inspection.q: When recording a defect, what information is most useful?
options: Exact location, size, description and photos
TI - Tank Inspection.why: Precise location, size and photos let the defect be assessed and repaired correctly.

TI - Tank Inspection.q: Coating condition in ballast tanks is commonly rated by class as what?
options: Grade A, B, C or D
TI - Tank Inspection.why: IACS and class surveys rate ballast tank coating condition as good, fair or poor.

TI - Tank Inspection.q: Why should ventilation continue while people are inside the tank?
options: To keep the air safe as conditions can change
TI - Tank Inspection.why: Continuous ventilation keeps oxygen levels safe and removes gases released during the work.

TI - Tank Inspection.q: What type of lighting should be used inside a tank that may contain flammable vapours?
TI - Tank Inspection.why: Intrinsically safe lighting cannot ignite flammable vapours.

VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.why: VOC means Volatile Organic Compound, a vapour released from petroleum cargoes.

VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.q: Which MARPOL Annex covers VOC emissions from tankers?
VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.why: MARPOL Annex VI, which deals with air pollution, includes the regulation on VOC from tankers.

VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.q: Which tankers must carry an approved VOC Management Plan?
options: Chemical tankers carrying only vegetable oils
VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.why: MARPOL Annex VI requires tankers carrying crude oil to have an approved VOC Management Plan.

VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.q: When are VOCs mainly released from a tanker?
options: During loading, transport and crude oil washing
Only when the engine is stopped
VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.why: Cargo evaporation during loading, voyage and crude oil washing releases VOCs.

VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.q: What is the purpose of a vapour emission control system during loading?
options: To collect displaced vapour and send it ashore instead of to the air
VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.why: Vapour return systems collect vapour displaced by the incoming cargo and send it to shore.

VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.q: What environmental harm do VOC emissions contribute to?
VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.why: VOCs react in sunlight to form ground-level ozone and smog.

VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.q: Which health effect can result from breathing VOC vapours?
options: Headache, dizziness and, for some vapours like benzene, cancer risk
VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.why: VOC vapours can cause headaches and dizziness, and benzene is a known carcinogen.

VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.q: How can crew help reduce VOC emissions?
options: Open tank hatches often for ventilation
Follow the VOC plan and avoid unnecessary venting
Load at the maximum rate without monitoring
VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.why: Keeping the cargo system closed and following the VOC plan limits vapour losses.

VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.q: What device protects cargo tanks from over-pressure and vacuum?
VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.why: P/V valves release excess pressure or admit air to prevent tank damage.

VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.q: What should crew wear or carry when working near possible VOC vapour sources?
options: A personal gas detector and suitable PPE
VOC - Volatile Organic Compound.why: Personal gas monitors and PPE protect crew from toxic vapour exposure.

VP - Voyage Planning.q: According to IMO guidelines, what are the four stages of voyage planning?
VP - Voyage Planning.why: IMO Resolution A.893(21) sets the stages as appraisal, planning, execution and monitoring.

VP - Voyage Planning.q: Which SOLAS chapter requires a voyage plan before the ship sails?
VP - Voyage Planning.why: SOLAS Chapter V (Regulation 34) requires a voyage plan before proceeding to sea.

VP - Voyage Planning.q: What happens during the appraisal stage?
options: Steering the ship along the track
Gathering all relevant information about the voyage
VP - Voyage Planning.why: Appraisal means collecting and studying all information relevant to the intended voyage.

VP - Voyage Planning.q: Which publication is commonly used during voyage appraisal?
VP - Voyage Planning.why: Sailing directions, tide tables, lists of lights and notices to mariners are key planning sources.

VP - Voyage Planning.q: What is a no-go area in a voyage plan?
options: An area where the ship must not enter due to danger
VP - Voyage Planning.why: No-go areas are marked where depth or hazards make the water unsafe for the ship.

options: The point where the pilot boards
The point where the engine is stopped
The point where the anchor is dropped
The point where the rudder is put over to start a planned turn
VP - Voyage Planning.why: Starting the turn at the wheel-over point brings the ship onto the next track as planned.

VP - Voyage Planning.q: What is the purpose of contingency planning in a voyage plan?
options: To prepare safe actions such as emergency anchorages and abort points
To reduce the number of charts
VP - Voyage Planning.why: Contingency plans give ready options if something goes wrong during the voyage.

VP - Voyage Planning.q: Who approves the voyage plan on board?
VP - Voyage Planning.why: The voyage plan is usually prepared by the navigating officer and approved by the master.

options: The depth of water between the keel and the seabed
The height of the mast above water
VP - Voyage Planning.why: UKC is the water depth remaining below the keel, which must meet company minimums.

VP - Voyage Planning.q: How is the voyage plan monitored during execution?
options: By trusting the plan without checks
By regular position fixes and cross-checks against the planned track
VP - Voyage Planning.why: Frequent fixes compared with the planned track show any deviation early.

VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.q: How often are Admiralty Notices to Mariners published?
VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.why: Admiralty Notices to Mariners are published weekly with chart and publication corrections.

VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.q: Where on an Admiralty paper chart is a small correction recorded?
options: On the back of the chart
VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.why: Small corrections are recorded in the bottom left-hand margin with the notice number and year.

VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.q: How are Temporary and Preliminary (T&P) notices usually marked on paper charts?
VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.why: T&P notices are marked in pencil so they can be removed when cancelled or made permanent.

VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.q: Before planning a voyage, what must be checked about the charts?
options: That they are the latest edition and fully corrected
That they are the cheapest available
That they are the smallest scale
VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.why: Only current, corrected charts give reliable navigational information.

VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.q: Which scale of chart should be used for coastal navigation and pilotage?
VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.why: Large-scale charts show the most detail needed for coastal waters.

VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.q: The Philippines is located in which NAVAREA for navigational warnings?
VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.why: The Philippines lies within NAVAREA XI, coordinated by Japan.

VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.q: How are ENC charts on ECDIS kept up to date?
options: By loading official update files and checking update status
VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.why: ENCs are corrected by applying official electronic updates and verifying they are installed.

VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.q: Which systems are used to receive navigational warnings at sea?
VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.why: NAVTEX and SafetyNET deliver navigational and meteorological warnings to ships.

VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.q: Why is a chart correction log kept on board?
options: To track which corrections have been applied to each chart
VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.why: A correction record proves charts are up to date and shows any missing corrections.

VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.q: What should be done with a relevant navigational warning when planning a route?
options: Mark it on the chart and adjust the plan if needed
Ignore it until it becomes permanent
VPCC - Voyage Planning and Chart Correct.why: Warnings affect safety, so they are plotted and considered in the voyage plan.

options: Knowing what is happening around you and what may happen next
VRM - Vessel Resource Management.why: Situational awareness means perceiving, understanding and predicting the situation.

options: A list of crew mistakes for punishment
A series of small errors that can lead to an accident
VRM - Vessel Resource Management.why: Accidents often result from linked errors; breaking the chain prevents the accident.

VRM - Vessel Resource Management.q: What should a junior officer do if he believes the master's order is unsafe?
options: Speak up clearly and explain the concern
VRM - Vessel Resource Management.why: Challenge and response encourages juniors to voice safety concerns respectfully.

options: Talking only to people you like
The receiver repeats the message and the sender confirms it
VRM - Vessel Resource Management.why: Repeating back and confirming messages ensures they are understood correctly.

VRM - Vessel Resource Management.q: Which resources does Vessel Resource Management cover?
VRM - Vessel Resource Management.why: VRM makes the best use of all available resources, including people, equipment, information and time.

VRM - Vessel Resource Management.q: What is the best leadership approach on board?
options: Adapt the style to the situation and team
Let the crew do whatever they want
VRM - Vessel Resource Management.why: Effective leaders adjust their style, being directive in emergencies and consultative when time allows.

VRM - Vessel Resource Management.q: How can workload be managed during busy periods?
options: Prioritise tasks and delegate to team members
VRM - Vessel Resource Management.why: Prioritising and delegating spreads the workload and keeps attention on critical tasks.

VRM - Vessel Resource Management.q: Why is a briefing held before a critical operation?
options: So everyone understands the plan, roles and risks
VRM - Vessel Resource Management.why: Briefings create a shared understanding of the plan, roles and hazards.

options: Overconfidence that leads to less care and attention
VRM - Vessel Resource Management.why: Complacency makes people relax their guard and miss warning signs.

VRM - Vessel Resource Management.q: What is the purpose of a debriefing after an operation?
options: To review what went well and what can be improved
VRM - Vessel Resource Management.why: Debriefings turn experience into lessons that improve future operations.

WH - Working at Heights.q: On board, working aloft is commonly defined as work above what height where a person could fall?
WH - Working at Heights.why: Common shipboard guidance treats work more than 2 metres above a deck as work at height.

WH - Working at Heights.q: What equipment should a person working at height wear for fall protection?
options: A full body harness with a lanyard attached to a secure anchor
A waist belt tied to a handrail
WH - Working at Heights.why: A full body harness attached to a strong anchor point arrests a fall safely.

WH - Working at Heights.q: When should a safety harness be inspected?
WH - Working at Heights.why: Harnesses are checked before every use for cuts, worn stitching and damaged buckles.

WH - Working at Heights.q: Where is the best position for an anchor point?
options: Above the worker and strong enough to hold a fall
WH - Working at Heights.why: An overhead anchor reduces fall distance and swing.

WH - Working at Heights.q: How can dropped objects be prevented when working aloft?
options: Secure tools with lanyards and barricade the area below
Ask people below to watch out
WH - Working at Heights.why: Tethering tools and keeping the area below clear protects people from falling objects.

WH - Working at Heights.q: What should be in place before starting work at height?
options: Only verbal permission from a friend
Nothing if the job is short
A risk assessment and a permit to work
WH - Working at Heights.why: Work at height is high-risk and must be assessed and authorised with a permit.

WH - Working at Heights.q: Why must a rescue plan be ready before work at height begins?
options: Because the job will be faster
A worker hanging in a harness needs prompt rescue to avoid suspension trauma
WH - Working at Heights.why: Prolonged suspension in a harness can cause serious injury, so rescue must be quick.

WH - Working at Heights.q: When climbing a ladder, how many points of contact should be kept?
WH - Working at Heights.why: Keeping three points of contact (two hands and a foot, or two feet and a hand) prevents falls.

WH - Working at Heights.q: A portable ladder should be set at about what angle?
WH - Working at Heights.why: The 1-in-4 rule gives an angle of about 75 degrees for stability.

WH - Working at Heights.q: What should be done with a harness that has arrested a fall?
options: Give it to another crew member
Remove it from service and report it
Keep it in the store as a spare
WH - Working at Heights.why: A harness that has taken a fall load may be weakened and must not be reused.
